Near the break, continuing the last ratio beat the curve on both runs (T1b failed: 0.26 against 0.77, and 0.17 against 0.24, at one day).
predictions.rival_en: Two causes the data cannot separate: the smooth class understating the need next to the fold, or a worsening regime lowering giving below what the same condition gives in a constant one. The paper's tipping days were read before the freeze, which expected T2-DF and T1b-DF to fail. Under day indexing shifted by one, the sucrose onsets agree (day 22 against 20).

predictions.label: C1, L
predictions.says_en: At a constant dilution of 500, the constant group's median reading (days 5–21) is within a factor 1.15 of the 2012 curve's level (C1), and the curve's one-day residuals, demeaned per population, carry less than 0.3 from one day to the next (L, the verdict 02's T2 text reads).

ifs.what_en: the control files, not named in the data's README, are the paper's constant group (DF 500, 2% sucrose)

predictions.seen_en: C1: 1.54 against the curve's 1.66, 8% apart. L: lag-1 autocorrelation −0.14 over 300 pairs.
predictions.rival_en: 02's T2 text: these residuals are at one constant dilution, never past the fold, outside the settings T2's 'Refuted by' names; the runs past the fold measured none of T2's forbidden items.

cases.afterwards_en: 21 October 2026: the margin-of-a-regime record's scope and next step were revised; its 'Does not show' now says a margin does not time a break (yeast driven past its fold broke three and at least six days before the curve from constant regimes said). T1's evidence lists MQ6 among its failures (3 of 10 passed). The README records the lesson as MQ1's again: read the instrument's floor before freezing a fate rule. Open: a renewal curve measured next to the fold, and a constant regime held at the deteriorating run's last condition before the break, to separate the two causes.
cases.shows_en: With the draw set from outside and the level the state at a constant dilution, the curve timed neither break: both came early, where the fold is least well measured.
cases.shows_zh: 抽取由外部设定，恒定稀释下水平就是状态，这些“如果”都成立，曲线仍没算准两次崩溃的时间：都来得更早，问题出在临界点附近量得最不准。

cases.case_en: A scripted market of renewing and extracting practices, with a collectible liability, paid influence that erodes it, a funded correction and a support stock; twelve runs of up to 800 rounds from chosen starts.
cases.case_zh: 一个用脚本写成的市场：有养护的做法和只取不养的做法，有可追收的罚责、花钱买来并削弱罚责的影响、有经费的纠正和一份支撑存量；从选定的起点跑十二次，每次至多八百轮。

things.thing_en: the renewing practice and the extracting practice, with the renewing share x
the private profit difference between the two practices (fine times accountability q, plus the lobbying cost, less the renewal cost), which drives payoff-led switching
the productive support stock C (renewal 2, extraction depletion 1, depreciation 1/10, floor 5)
the renewing practice's paid maintenance
the extracting practice
the market's production and payments, which stop for good once an essential support fails
the excluded nonessential recipient, whose support can fall below its floor while the market goes on
the liquid correction fund B (levy in, restoration fee out, cap 3)

bridges.name: market correspondence
bridges.claim_en: An actual market is taken to follow the model's supplied laws: fixed demand, payoff-driven switching, truthful classification of liable practices, protected floors, installed authority, influence conversion and the physical renewal law.
bridges.why_en: The README: 'These are supplied local economic and physical laws, not empirical market data or a completed derivation of institutions from the generative foundation.' The home record's Does not show: 'That an actual market meets the model: parameters, laws and correspondence are supplied.'

bridges.name: roles in the model
bridges.claim_en: In the script the two practices are what payments select among, the support stock is what production depends on, and accountability q is the setting of the selecting rule.
bridges.why_en: The model is written so; the formal guide adds that 'naming someone in the protected vector remains a substantive supplied choice'.

bridges.name: rule revised by paid influence
bridges.claim_en: Paid influence from political spending eroding accountability, and funded correction restoring it, is taken as a selection rule set from what it selected.
bridges.why_en: The response coefficient lambda is supplied: the model 'does not derive influence technology'; correction is 'an already authorized policy' and 'this is not a model of learning which rule to install'.

bridges.name: simulator to Lean
bridges.claim_en: The Python simulator's operating histories are taken as the Lean-checked model's.
bridges.why_en: 'The safe-history claims agree on the operating trajectories, but no Python-to-Lean refinement theorem is claimed.' The independent reconstruction checks the Python implementation against separately written equations, not against the Lean: 2,187 rectangle points, 21,600 broader domain/accounting points, 48 exact short-history steps and three independently derived exact witnesses.

predictions.label: Renewal region and bounded adverse shocks (saved comparison; nothing frozen)
predictions.says_en: From a start inside the proved rectangle (renewing share at least 3/4, accountability at least 1/2, influence at most 1/4, fund from 1 to 3, support at least 5) no support failure at any round, also under accountability disturbances up to 1/20 and support losses up to 1/2 a round.

ifs.what_en: the start (share 4/5, accountability 3/5, influence 1/5, fund 1, support 8) lies in the rectangle and the disturbances (1/20 and 1/2 a round) are within the admitted bounds
the Python step is the Lean step (no refinement theorem; an independent reconstruction of the Python agrees with it)

predictions.seen_en: Renewal region: no economic failure through 800 rounds. Bounded adverse shocks: none through 800; 'Supports remain above admitted floors'. The README: 'Consistent with the invariant and attraction proofs'.
predictions.rival_en: 05 §10: 'An equation-identical conventional controller predicts the same'.

predictions.label: Capture region and its three comparators (saved comparison; nothing frozen)
predictions.says_en: From the destructive region (share at most 1/10, accountability at most 9/25, influence at least 9/10) the support crosses its floor although restoration stays funded. Lean checks only that this low box is kept at every time; the finite failure is the mathematical study's (its support bound C_t <= (C_0+7)0.9^t - 7 while production continues). Lean's own finite-failure theorem (RegimeAttraction.low_guarded_history_fails) is for a share at most 1/48 and does not reach this start's 2/25.

ifs.what_en: the start (share 2/25, accountability 7/20, influence 19/20, fund 1, support 100) lies in the destructive region
correction is paid at every round until failure (21 paid rounds)
the Python step is the Lean step (no refinement theorem)

predictions.seen_en: Capture region: first economic failure at round 21. Same start with the capture coefficient zero: none through 800. Rule frozen at its initial low value: 21 ('Fixed bad selection also fails; endogenous capture is not the only failure mechanism'). Ideal fixed accountability: none through 800.
predictions.rival_en: A rule frozen low fails at the same round, so endogenous capture is not the only route; an equation-identical conventional controller predicts the same.

predictions.label: No renewing variant initially (saved comparison; nothing frozen)
predictions.says_en: A renewing share of none stays none: selection does not create an absent practice.

ifs.what_en: the renewing share starts at 0 (the capture region's start otherwise)

predictions.seen_en: The saved trajectory's renewing share is zero at every saved round; first economic failure at round 19. The README: 'The switching law creates no absent variant'.

predictions.label: Excluded nonessential recipient (saved comparison; nothing frozen)
predictions.says_en: A recipient not named essential can be harmed while the market keeps operating. The Lean witness is a neighbouring built state, one step from both supports at 5; the saved run starts the productive support at 20 and the recipient's at 5, for 800 rounds.

ifs.what_en: the recipient's support is in the state but not designated essential

predictions.seen_en: No economic failure through 800 rounds; 'Recipient support violates its floor in round 1 despite stable production'.

predictions.label: Levy one half of the intervention cost (saved comparison; nothing frozen)
predictions.says_en: No prediction: the proved every-round funding rectangle takes a levy at least the correction's cost; this run sets the levy at half of it.

ifs.what_en: levy at least the correction's cost (tau >= k), as the proved rectangle takes

predictions.seen_en: No economic failure through 800 rounds; 400 interventions are paid. The README: tau>=k 'is sufficient for the proved every-round funding rectangle, not necessary for all surviving histories'; the survival 'is numerical evidence within the synthetic law; a separate intermittent-funding invariant has not been proved'.

predictions.label: Exact checks and independent reconstruction
predictions.says_en: The one-step rectangle, the cash identities and the long runs come out the same when recomputed exactly and by a reconstruction that imports neither implementation.

ifs.what_en: the reconstruction is written from the equations without importing model.py or run.py

predictions.seen_en: 2,187 rational one-step rectangle checks, cash identities, seven named finite examples and five violated-boundary counterexamples; twelve 800-round runs at 80-digit precision recomputed at 120 digits, 48,861 scalar comparisons within the declared tolerance of 10^-68; observed maximum discrepancy approximately 2.979 x 10^-78, which 'reflects finite precision, not empirical uncertainty'.

cases.afterwards_en: From 8 October 2026 further Lean modules were checked on the same model: the regime boundary (19 theorems), local attraction and coupled support (38), a finite transition with support (27), partial correction (26) and the finite-support obstruction (17); MarketInstances joins the model to the pure core's theorems on lasting and viability (05 §10). 08 §8's assessment: 'A conventional controller with identical equations predicts exactly the same results, so the theory's vocabulary adds no mathematical advantage there.' The test's row names no thesis; 05 keeps as open a discriminating study in one bounded market.
cases.shows_en: Here reasoning meets only a case built to its own premises: the runs agree with the proofs, no market data enters, and an equation-identical conventional controller predicts the same.
cases.shows_zh: 推理在这里只遇到按它自己的前提造出来的例子：运行与证明一致，没有任何市场数据，一个方程相同的常规控制器给出同样的结果。

cases.case_en: Binned data on how far people's eyes jumped (saccade adaptation), in two groups of twenty, while correcting jumps cost viewing time for a motion judgment; in one group the cost switched sides at trial 951.
cases.case_zh: 别人公开的眼跳适应分箱数据，两组各二十人：纠正性的眼跳会占掉看运动点做判断的时间；其中一组在第951次试验时，两侧的代价对调。

things.thing_en: a participant's primary-saccade amplitude relative to baseline, in degrees, as it adapts
the 300-ms viewing period after a primary saccade, part of which corrective movements consume
corrective saccades
the motion judgment on the dots, whose low or high coherence sets what losing viewing time costs

bridges.name: label mapping
bridges.claim_en: The workbook's LARGE COST and SMALL COST series are taken as the initial physical sides throughout the recorded series.
bridges.why_en: 'this mapping is not independently verified by a raw side-tag dictionary'; the outputs keep the literal source labels and the secure estimand is 'the literal source-series contrast'.

bridges.name: cost alone
bridges.claim_en: The coherence switch at trial 951 is taken as a change in what an error costs, and nothing else.
bridges.why_en: Both sides reverse, so EXP2 'has no untreated opposite side'; the evidence audit: 'Changing task coherence also changes sensory demands and consequences, so our contrast is not a measured isolated resource effect.'

bridges.name: no-switch comparator
bridges.claim_en: The EXP1 group is taken as what the EXP2 group would have done without the switch.
bridges.why_en: 'EXP1 is a separate no-switch cohort, not a randomized within-person counterfactual for EXP2'; shared ID numerals do not pair people across experiments.

bridges.name: paid route-revision branch
bridges.claim_en: To bear on the paid route-revision branch, a change in the response curves after the cost switch would have to be taken as a change in the retained component that does the updating; the test does not take it so.
bridges.why_en: The README: 'not evidence that a biological learning-rule component was replaced'; the identification analysis 'shows why changing a fitted gain, delivered input, available writing or hidden memory can produce similar observations'; 'this workbook does not supply those measurements'.

predictions.label: Primary: EXP2 early
predictions.says_en: The protocol fixed the primary estimand, the mean contrast C early after the switch in the switch group, and how it reads: negative values 'indicate that the initially small-cost side, which becomes costly, shortens its saccade more than the side whose cost falls'. The evidence audit calls negative 'the expected opposed-switch direction'. Fixed before the new contrasts but after the source's conclusions were known; 'not a preregistration'; no threshold decides.

ifs.what_en: the LARGE/SMALL labels are the initial physical sides
the switch changes the cost of an error and nothing else

predictions.seen_en: Mean -0.181722 degrees, 95% interval [-0.453318, 0.089873], n=20; the SMALL series changes by -0.398970 degrees and LARGE by -0.217248. 'The primary estimate is negative but its interval includes zero.'
predictions.rival_en: A condition-dependent gain, a changed delivered input, a writing gate or hidden memory can give similar observations; coherence also changes sensory demands.

predictions.label: Secondary: EXP2 late
predictions.says_en: The same contrast in the late window, fixed as secondary; a negative value has the same reading.

ifs.what_en: the LARGE/SMALL labels are the initial physical sides

predictions.seen_en: Mean -0.340414 degrees, 95% interval [-0.593631, -0.087197], n=20. 'more clearly separated from zero under the declared sampling models'; 'they do not replace the primary'.
predictions.rival_en: These are response-trajectory contrasts: they 'neither estimate a trial-level learning gain nor establish a cost-only causal effect or a changed retained updater'.

predictions.label: Secondary: EXP1 early and late (no-switch group)
predictions.says_en: The same contrasts in the no-switch group, fixed for report; no direction stated.

predictions.label: Secondary: EXP2 minus EXP1, between groups
predictions.says_en: Fixed as a descriptive difference of within-person differences between independent groups; no direction or threshold stated.

ifs.what_en: the two groups are exchangeable, with parallel counterfactual trends

predictions.rival_en: 'A causal interpretation of the cohort difference would additionally require an adequate assignment/counterfactual design.'

predictions.label: Independent numerical check
predictions.says_en: A separate estimator, reading the workbook's XML and fixed before comparing outcomes, gives the same numbers as the producer.

ifs.what_en: the independent estimator was fixed before comparing outcomes with the producer

predictions.seen_en: Matches 2,000 source values, 2,000 coordinate occurrences, 240 window means, 160 component changes, 80 participant contrasts and 112 aggregate fields; maximum absolute numerical discrepancy 7.1x10^-15.

cases.afterwards_en: The test's row names no thesis. The same day's identification analysis (6 October 2026) sets out the alternatives that give similar observations, and the README names what the next claim needs: 'an independently specified retained component and matched input/write/readout interventions; this workbook does not supply those measurements.'
cases.shows_en: No theorem is named here: a contrast fixed in advance came out negative with an interval including zero, and binned response curves cannot show whether the learner's own updating changed.
cases.shows_zh: 这里没有点名任何定理：事先定好的对比结果为负，但区间包含零；分箱的反应曲线也看不出学习者自身的更新方式是否变了。

cases.case_en: Walleye lakes of Wisconsin's Ceded Territory, read through WDNR's and GLIFWC's records: spring adult estimates with intervals, fall surveys of age-0 fish, harvest, stocking, and each lake's recruitment-source label.
cases.case_zh: 威斯康星州让与地内的大眼梭鲈湖，用州自然资源部和五大湖印第安渔猎委员会的记录来读：带区间的春季成鱼估数、秋季当年幼鱼调查、捕捞、放流，以及各湖的补充来源标签。

things.thing_en: a lake's adult walleye per acre, by spring mark-and-recapture estimates
the fall's age-0 walleye, which join the adults about three years later
the harvest, tribal and angling
stocking, and fish arriving from connected waters

bridges.name: T1
bridges.claim_en: Walleye lakes are taken as a condition whose renewal stops below a need, drawn on by harvest and closed but for stocking.
bridges.why_en: The run refused before any value: 'no need is measured, and nothing is said of T1'. The design's own limits: the need is the 50% point, where renewal is 'rarer than at it, not stopped', and 'T1's regime has no lag' where walleye join the adults about three years on.

bridges.name: the need (DESIGN §4)
bridges.claim_en: The adult density at which the fitted chance of a fall survey catching at least one age-0 per mile is one half, fitted on lake-years up to 2012, is taken as T1's need.
bridges.why_en: No fit was made. Counted from structure alone after the refusal, the fit 'could have about 162 lake-years as the fall tables were read, where it needs 200': about 162 from 101 lakes, against a minimum of 200 from at least 30 lakes.

bridges.name: giving from beyond (DESIGN §5)
bridges.claim_en: Recorded stocking, a natural-recruitment label and a seepage lake type are taken to show whether anything was given to a lake from beyond.
bridges.why_en: R5b and R7 were not fetched. The stocking database as found holds 13,813 rows of walleye and includes what §3 expected it to leave out: 1,160 rows of fry, 2,105 of private stocking and 844 of other governments'.

bridges.name: the need alone (DESIGN §7)
bridges.claim_en: The need alone, not T1's point of no return under a standing draw, is taken as the predicted point.
bridges.why_en: The design sets V1 so and argues it: 'Here the draw does not stand: safe harvests are set from each lake's estimates, so the harvest is cut as a lake falls'; 'Below the need, T1 predicts a fall under any draw, so V1 reads the need alone'. V1 does not read the harvest.

bridges.name: R1's layout (DESIGN §9)
bridges.claim_en: The agency's public table of adult estimates is taken to give, per lake and year, the estimate, both interval bounds and the lake's acres.
bridges.why_en: The run's output: "adult_estimates.csv lacks ['Acres', 'Upper 95 C.I.']". The table also holds WDNR's estimates alone, where §3 named WDNR and GLIFWC; §9 'had taken the columns from a search engine's summary and assumed the rest'.

predictions.label: V1, the separation (primary)
predictions.says_en: Lakes read wholly below the need, with no year class pending from the three falls before, decline by a ratio test on the recorders' own intervals, not undone by a recovery, at least the critical count of an exact one-sided sign test at 0.05 (9 of 10, 11 of 14, 15 of 20), and more often than lakes above the need by Fisher's exact test at 0.05. Refuted where at most n - c fell, or at most half of twenty or more, always with a clause on estimates distorted at low density.

ifs.what_en: the public table of adult estimates gives, per lake and year, the estimate, both interval bounds and the acres (the header was read; no upper bound and no acres column)
a need is found: at least 200 lake-year pairs from at least 30 lakes up to 2012, the fit converging, the slope's lower 95% bound above zero, at least 20 lake-years on either side
the lake was shown above the need before the cutoff: two estimates up to 2012, at most ten years apart, with lower bounds at or above it, no decline between, label natural, no stocking recorded
nothing given from beyond between the reference and the fate: no stocking recorded, the label still natural

at least 10 lakes read below the need with a resolved fate (counted from structure after the refusal, outside the freeze: at most 9 on the published table with the stocking database as the frozen reader reads them; other readings give 10 or 13)
T1's draw stands, not cut as the level falls

predictions.rival_en: Renewal lost for years to another cause (habitat, warming) or in long chance spells gives the same positive outcome, in up to 40 of 40 dry-run archives; so the positive line adds 'the need's causal role not shown' and is 'not "T1 supported"'.

predictions.label: V2, a return from below the need (reported beside V1, deciding nothing)
predictions.says_en: T1 forbids a lake below its need, every year of the lag surveyed with none at the floor, coming back to or above the need with no recorded stocking and its label natural throughout; any such lake is listed.

ifs.what_en: no unrecorded stocking, no fish from connected waters, no cohort the floor missed

predictions.rival_en: 'An unrecorded stocking, fish from connected waters, a cohort the floor missed or the estimates' error could produce it', so it is 'listed beside V1, not a verdict'.

predictions.label: Renewal below the need after 2012 (reported)
predictions.says_en: Among lake-years after 2012 with an estimate wholly below the need, renewal reaches the floor no more often than the need's fit expects; more, at 0.05, means the need moved or the fit misplaced it.

ifs.what_en: a need is fitted on the years up to 2012

predictions.label: Dry run on synthetic lakes (before the freeze)
predictions.says_en: The frozen rules, the reader, the run and the freeze's chain behave as designed on synthetic archives: 48 worlds at four speeds of the managers' response, three of them again at 900 lakes.

ifs.what_en: the archives are built by dry_run.py: 300 lakes, 1990 to 2025, adults estimated every three to five years

predictions.seen_en: 238 checks, none failed, 319 CPU seconds. LAYOUT.md afterwards: the dry run 'tested the rules against the worlds, and could not show what R1's own structure allows'.

cases.afterwards_en: Refused at its one run on 6 November 2026, at R1's header, before reading a row. LAYOUT.md then counted from structure alone, outside the freeze: at most 9 lakes where V1 needs 10, and about 162 lake-years from 101 lakes where the need's fit needs 200; with GLIFWC's estimates added (at most 31 lakes) and T1N's own worlds put on that grid, V1 was decided in 1 of 1,200 archives and never in T1's own world. T1R, which imports T1N's need, refused at the same header. The design had expected 'not decided' as the likeliest answer. T1B, a successor with different rules, is named on the board and held by Ren since 6 November 2026. Nothing is said of T1; 08 §9's evidence for T1 still ends 'no field test of a need measured in advance'.
cases.shows_en: The frozen rules never reached a value: the public table lacked an upper bound and acres, so the run refused, and nothing is said of T1.
cases.shows_zh: 冻结的规则没有读到任何数值：公开的表里没有区间上界，也没有面积一栏，运行就此拒绝，对T1什么也没说。

cases.case_en: Twenty-four rats, each in two seven-minute sessions, could pull to give food access to a partner that did not cooperate, while smelling another rat elsewhere that was either helping or had no pulling stick.
cases.case_zh: 二十四只大鼠，各做两场七分钟的测试：它可以拉杆让一只不合作的同伴够到食物，同时闻到别处另一只大鼠的气味，那只要么正在帮忙，要么没有拉杆可用。

things.thing_en: the focal rat, which can pull to give its partner access to food
the noncooperative recipient facing the focal rat
the odour reaching the focal rat from another rat elsewhere
the odour provider's assigned situation: helping, or with no pulling-stick access

bridges.name: pulls as recipient-directed actions
bridges.claim_en: A pull is taken as a recipient-directed food-access action, and the difference in pulls as a difference in such actions between the two odour situations.
bridges.why_en: It is so by the source experiment's apparatus, not checked here: 'Training, apparatus, repeated exposure and treatment assignment are supplied by the experiment.' The conceptual review 'accepts the scoped implementation and interpretation'; counts are 'not independently verified ingestion, welfare, energy expenditure or survival'.

bridges.name: cue as cooperation alone
bridges.claim_en: The odour situation is taken as the provider's cooperation and nothing else.
bridges.why_en: 'That situation bundles cooperation with stick access, activity and other possible state changes.' The same odour provider was used in both situations, so a fixed identity-only account is 'a narrower comparator'.

bridges.name: cue → recipient-directed action (PROTOCOL's connection)
bridges.claim_en: More pulls under the cooperating odour are taken as sensitivity to the odour provider's assigned situation: an externally acquired cue used in a recipient-directed action.
bridges.why_en: The plan reads a positive contrast so 'conditional on design assumptions', which the preview cannot estimate. How acquired information is bound to the one affected is named as 'the next bridge', not shown here: 'It does not identify recipient-specific reasoning, an identity mistake, moral concern or a solution to alignment'; 'No delayed memory test or alternative-beneficiary choice occurs here.'

bridges.name: the preview as the data
bridges.claim_en: The 48 displayed rows of the public preview, all 24 pairs, are taken as experiment 4's data.
bridges.why_en: 'Original CSV downloads failed, so original file bytes were not verified'; the visible rendering was checked (3119 canonical ASCII bytes). 'The published result uses n=23', an 'unexplained sample-size discrepancy'.

predictions.label: Primary paired count contrast
predictions.says_en: No prediction of the account. The plan fixed the contrast, cooperating minus neutral pulls per focal rat, a positive value to be read as sensitivity to the provider's assigned situation; the totals (21 and 53 pulls; 17 increases, four decreases, three ties) were known before the plan was frozen.

ifs.what_en: the animals are comparable independent units: no shared donors, common influences or carryover
the displayed preview is the original data

predictions.seen_en: 24 complete pairs; neutral 21 pulls (mean 0.875), cooperating 53 (mean 2.2083); mean paired difference 1.3333, median 1, sample SD 1.7110; 17 increasing, 4 decreasing, 3 tied; zero-count sessions 10 neutral, 4 cooperating.
predictions.rival_en: 'Cue-triggered helping, generalized reciprocity and richer recipient models remain possible'; the contrast 'does not identify a unique cognitive mechanism'.

predictions.label: Bootstrap interval and exact reference probabilities
predictions.says_en: Fixed calculations under stated assumptions; 'No threshold determines conceptual acceptance'.

ifs.what_en: sign symmetry or exchangeability of the paired differences; the actual assignment probabilities, restrictions and carryover

predictions.seen_en: Exploratory 95% animal-paired bootstrap interval for the mean difference [0.6667, 2.0000] (20,000 resamples). Paired-sign reference 24496 / 16777216 = 0.0014600754; binomial sign reference 15094 / 2097152 = 0.0071973801 among 21 nontied pairs. They are 'not recovered assignment-exact randomization probabilities'.

predictions.label: Every single-animal omission
predictions.says_en: The descriptive estimates and both reference calculations repeated with each of the 24 animals left out in turn; no omission is to be preferred or used to recover the published n=23.
predictions.seen_en: Mean differences range from 1.1739 to 1.4783 additional pulls; paired-sign reference probabilities from 0.00035095 to 0.00291824; binomial sign references from 0.00257683 to 0.01181793. 'No omission is selected or treated as explaining the published sample size.'

predictions.label: Latency coding audit
predictions.says_en: The plan: report whether a session with no pull shows the displayed first-pull timing 420, which is not to be treated as an observed event; no latency estimate is calculated.
predictions.seen_en: All 14 zero-count sessions display 420; all 34 positive-count sessions have first timings from 6 to 389 seconds; two Pull6 cells (preview rows 39 and 41) are NA and stay missing. The article's latency Wilcoxon p=.003 and supplementary Cox p=.048 'remain an unresolved discrepancy'.

predictions.label: Independent numerical check
predictions.says_en: A separate checker reading the preserved table, with a distinct enumeration, reproduces the pairs, the arithmetic, the exact probabilities and the bootstrap replay.
predictions.seen_en: 'all source cells, paired arithmetic, bootstrap replay and 50 exact reference calculations across the full sample and all omissions match'. The receipt's scope: an arithmetic audit of a derived preview, with 'no original-CSV verification or validation of sampling, assignment or cognitive interpretation assumptions'.

cases.afterwards_en: The test's row names no thesis. The plan names the next bridge: 'identifying how acquired information is bound to an affected center and used through effective action despite cue/source/recipient mismatch'. The executable result keeps its original status, computed_pending_independent_review; a separate receipt and a review record the later acceptance.
cases.shows_en: No theorem is named and the totals were known before the plan: the rats pulled 1.33 more times per session under the cooperating smell, which several accounts would give.
cases.shows_zh: 这里没有点名定理，总数在计划定下之前就已知道：闻到合作气味时，大鼠每场多拉1.33次，而好几种解释都会给出同样的结果。

cases.case_en: In released choice records of a 2020 laboratory study, male rats chose between two food levers; for 12 the preferred lever then also shocked a neighbouring rat, for 14 it did not.
cases.case_zh: 一项2020年大鼠实验的公开记录：雄鼠在两根给食杠杆之间选择；其中12只的偏好杠杆此后会同时电击邻鼠，另外14只的不会。

things.thing_en: a male rat's free choice between its two food levers (20 baseline opportunities, 60 over three later sessions)
the two levers: the one the rat preferred at baseline, and the other
footshocks to the neighbouring rat that follow the preferred lever

bridges.name: named connection (PROTOCOL)
bridges.claim_en: A rat's later lever choice, once its preferred lever also shocks its neighbour, is taken as an action that has acquired a harmful consequence for another animal while the offered food return stays the same.
bridges.why_en: Offered food stays equal (one pellet per response on either lever), but realized food, effort and the rat's own aversive experience are not fixed, and the free-choice log does not identify total shocks or separately verify what the neighbour experienced.

bridges.name: comparison groups
bridges.claim_en: The 12 contingent-harm and 14 no-harm male rats of the released trial file are taken as alike but for the shock.
bridges.why_en: Group assignment randomization and cage identity are not established, and SBL record labels do not overlap between the two groups; so no randomization p-value or population confidence interval is claimed.

bridges.name: to the concern model of that time (v = gw)
bridges.claim_en: The larger fall in preferred-lever responses is taken as the neighbour's harm coming to influence the rat's choice.
bridges.why_en: The README: an observed change can reflect contingency learning applied to an existing aversion; it does not identify that aversion's origin or separate learned value from correspondence. Actual relief of the neighbour against relief of the rat's own cue is the missing discriminator.

bridges.name: to the present account
bridges.claim_en: The case is taken as bearing on the generative account of 6 October 2026, now in history; no thesis, Lean theorem or atlas dynamic of the present account is bound to it.
bridges.why_en: tests.json lists it under no prediction of the account; no binding or dynamic names it. The role ids under 'things' are an AI reading by the web's reaches tie, not the record's.

predictions.label: primary contrast: male contingent harm minus male no harm
predictions.says_en: A frozen contrast with no direction scored: the difference between 12 contingent-harm and 14 no-harm male rats in the mean within-rat change of preferred-lever responses per offered free choice. The named connection is that lever choice changes once the lever also shocks the neighbour, offered food unchanged; the published direction was already known.

ifs.what_en: The two groups differ only in the shock (random assignment, cage identity, cohort)
The offered food is the same on both levers, one pellet per response (the laboratory's design, read from the paper's methods)

Apart from the shock to the neighbour, nothing changes for the rat itself between baseline and the later sessions (lever forces differ between levers but are fixed within a rat; realized food and its own distress at the neighbour's cues are not fixed)

predictions.seen_en: -16.69 percentage points (-841/5040): harm group 72.92% to 51.11% (-21.81 pp), no-harm group 81.07% to 75.95% (-5.12 pp). Decomposition: preferred -16.69 pp, alternative +16.41 pp, nonperformance +0.28 pp; completed-choice contrast -16.50 pp. Reported as descriptive, with no p-value or population interval.
predictions.rival_en: Contingency learning applied to an existing aversion; relief of the rat's own cue distress rather than the neighbour's relief; cohort differences between groups whose record labels do not overlap; regression from a preference defined at baseline.

predictions.label: influence analyses: leave one rat out, leave one SBL label out
predictions.says_en: Every single-rat omission and every omission of one recorded SBL label is computed for the primary contrast, as influence analyses, not corrections for cohort confounding; no pass criterion was fixed.
predictions.seen_en: Every omission keeps the primary contrast negative; the 6 October account gives -19.24 to -12.76 pp over single rats and -21.55 to -11.83 pp over SBL labels.

predictions.label: prior experience: rats shocked themselves beforehand minus rats never shocked
predictions.says_en: Contrast frozen in the protocol; the direction comes from the identification note, written before local aggregates with the published results known: if firsthand shock raises the rat's own learned aversion, its correspondence to the other is positive and unchanged, and efficacy beliefs and the private choice process are comparable, the neighbour's harm moves choice more after firsthand shock.

ifs.what_en: Firsthand shock raised the rat's own learned aversion
The correspondence between own and other's condition is positive and unchanged
Efficacy beliefs and the private choice process are comparable between exposed and unexposed rats
Rats were randomly assigned between the two experience conditions

predictions.seen_en: The 12 exposed harm rats changed -21.81 pp, the 14 never-exposed -5.24 pp; change contrast -16.57 pp. The account calls it consistent with a contribution from firsthand aversive experience and says it does not isolate that mechanism: exposure precedes the recorded baseline, randomization is unverified and record labels differ.
predictions.rival_en: Shock experience can also teach the meaning of another's reactions, alter estimated personal danger, or increase generalized or context-conditioned fear; pre-existing aversion plus newly learned lever contingencies remains sufficient.

predictions.label: random harm (descriptive)
predictions.says_en: The eight random-harm rats' change is reported against the contingent-harm group and labelled separately; it is not a same-dose randomized contingency manipulation.

ifs.what_en: The random schedules match the contingent ones in dose and timing (by the paper's methods they were drawn from the eight strongest contingent-harm switchers, with shocks delayed into intertrial intervals)

predictions.seen_en: The random-harm group changed +1.04 pp, against -21.81 pp under contingent harm; its schedules came from the strongest switchers and its shocks were delayed into intertrial intervals.

predictions.label: unequal food (descriptive)
predictions.says_en: The 1-vs-2 and 1-vs-3 pellet groups are reported against the main one-pellet harm group as bounded cost patterns, not a pure food-price experiment.

ifs.what_en: The unequal-food groups differ from the main group only in food (by the paper's methods they use equal lever forces, and group histories differ)

predictions.seen_en: Preferred-lever responses changed -7.62 pp where that lever offered two pellets and -0.76 pp with three (one trial slot unknown, so a lower bound on the complete change), against -21.81 pp in the one-pellet group.

predictions.label: independent reconstruction
predictions.says_en: A separately written checker, parsing the original bytes without importing the producer, must reproduce every value, and deliberately corrupted copies must be rejected.
predictions.seen_en: 21,581 exact scalar comparisons pass (every rat, all 6,240 trial slots, seven groups, six contrasts, 780 source-summary audit entries); twelve corrupted variants rejected. 39 source audit flags are kept; all seven percentage or undefined flags lie outside the primary groups. Separate implementation by a collaborating AI, not independent collection.

cases.afterwards_en: The first producer run stopped on a literal NaN in the summary cross-check; the repair maps it to unknown and changed no selection, estimator or trial outcome. The account it fed (6 October 2026) is now in history. The identification argument names what is still missing: a contrast separating the neighbour's actual relief from the rat's own cue relief. No thesis or theorem changed.
cases.shows_en: On others' records, preferred-lever responses fell 16.69 points more where the lever shocked a neighbour; with no theorem bound, assignment unestablished and rivals unseparated, it stays descriptive.
cases.shows_zh: 在别人的记录上，偏好杠杆会电击邻鼠时，按压多降了16.69个百分点；没有绑定任何定理，分组是否随机没有证实，别的解释也没分开，所以只是描述。

cases.case_en: In Zhang and Hackel's Experiment 3 (2025), people were trained with a target's favourable states going with, or against, their own payoff, then chose 32 times between options the target liked or disliked.
cases.case_zh: 在 Zhang 与 Hackel 2025年的实验三里，受试者先受训：对象的好状态与自己的报酬同向或反向；然后做32次选择，一个选项对象喜欢，一个不喜欢。

things.thing_en: a participant's choice between the two options in each of 32 offered decisions
the two options of each decision: the one the target liked and the one it disliked
what the participant learned in training: the target's favourable states going with, or against, the participant's own payoff
the likes and dislikes of the target (a previous participant), as displayed to the participant

bridges.name: named connection (PROTOCOL section 1)
bridges.claim_en: Congruent reward training is taken as an acquired evaluation of another's state, and later target-liked selections as choice concerning that target.
bridges.why_en: The contrast remains uncertain around zero and warrants no directional behavioural claim; it neither establishes equivalence nor identifies the mechanism of acquired concern.

bridges.name: private payoff held fixed
bridges.claim_en: With the assigned decision-phase contingency held fixed, the participant's own expected payoff is taken as the same across training arms.
bridges.why_en: The protocol says holding the objective contingency fixed does not hold subjective expected private payoff fixed, and trial-level expectations were not independently measured. The identification argument gives a model in which a rise in target-directed evaluation can instead be placed in unobserved payoff expectation, with identical finite choice histories (a nonidentification result in a stated model class, not a diagnosis of these participants).

bridges.name: the observed sample
bridges.claim_en: The 333 author-eligible participants are taken to stand for all who were randomized.
bridges.why_en: Post-assignment exclusions (52 of 385 matched respondents; five completed surveys without usable IDs not recovered) prevent an unconditional intention-to-treat claim; results.json records full_randomized_ITT_identified: false.

bridges.name: recorded selection as benefit
bridges.claim_en: A recorded target-liked selection is taken as a choice that benefits the target.
bridges.why_en: The release establishes displayed instructions, recorded choices and feedback; no identified fulfilment ledger verifies actual gifts to the target or realized personal financial sacrifice.

bridges.name: bounded alternative (formal/)
bridges.claim_en: Data of this kind would meet the folder's own Lean bound on choice change under unchanged evaluation only with a validated score budget and paired coverage.
bridges.why_en: The current reward-learning archive supplies neither; the Lean (27 audited declarations in two modules) was added afterwards and reads no participant data.

bridges.name: to the present account
bridges.claim_en: The case is taken as bearing on the generative account of 6 October 2026, now in history; no thesis, Lean theorem of the Becoming package or atlas dynamic is bound to it.
bridges.why_en: tests.json lists it under no prediction of the account; no binding or dynamic names it. The role ids under 'things' are an AI reading (the trained association as a reading of the target's state), not the record's.

predictions.label: primary: standardized training contrast, author-eligible, 32 offered trials
predictions.says_en: One frozen contrast with no direction scored: congruent minus incongruent training in target-liked selections per 32 offered decisions, within each current payoff condition, the two weighted equally. The protocol says a nonzero contrast would support transfer from training to later target-liked responding, and nothing more.

ifs.what_en: Exclusions after assignment do not select the sample
The participant's subjective expected private payoff is the same across training arms

predictions.seen_en: +0.50 percentage points among 333 participants, approximate 95% interval -4.25 to +5.24; -0.38 points within the current congruent condition and +1.37 within the incongruent. Cell means of liked responses per 32: 84.41%, 84.79%, 53.89%, 52.52%. The interval is not an equivalence test and no equivalence margin was selected.
predictions.rival_en: Even a well-established transfer could come from acquired private-payoff expectations, target-state knowledge or task demands as well as target-directed valuation; a fixed concern weight with changed reward beliefs gives the same choices.

predictions.label: three fixed sensitivities
predictions.says_en: The same contrast for all 385 saved matched respondents, for an answered-trial denominator, and counting only responses of at least 0.2 seconds; intervals individually nominal, not simultaneous.
predictions.seen_en: All saved (385): -0.31 points [-4.90, +4.29]. Answered-trial denominator (333): +0.34 [-4.40, +5.09]. RT at least 0.2 s (333): +1.47 [-3.47, +6.40]. All three intervals contain zero.

predictions.label: coding reconciliation
predictions.says_en: On the offered-trial scale, the no-reversal minus reversal contrast in self-optimal choices must equal the primary contrast less half the response-fraction difference in the current incongruent condition.
predictions.seen_en: The optimal-choice contrast is +0.43 points, not the primary +0.50; the recorded response adjustment reconciles them (identity error -5.55e-17 in results.json). The paper's mixed-logistic model was not fitted.

predictions.label: independent numerical check
predictions.says_en: A checker that does not import the producer's calculation functions reconstructs eligibility and coding from source and recomputes the contrast and interval.
predictions.seen_en: 385 participants, 12,320 offered trials and all 10,532 published cleaned responses reconstructed; 6,160 participant fields, 98,560 offered-trial fields, 200 aggregate fields, 16 awareness fields and 412 hashes match; largest numerical difference 1.14e-13. Numerical acceptance, distinct from the scientific interpretation.

predictions.label: source reconciliation targets
predictions.says_en: The reconstruction must reach the counts found by the metadata-only audit: 387 task files, 390 completed surveys (five without usable IDs), 385 matched respondents, 333 eligible, 52 excluded; a discrepancy blocks execution.
predictions.seen_en: The counts were reached and every answered row of the published cleaned data reconciled. One descriptive discrepancy stays unresolved: the released eligible records give 145 aware and 188 unaware participants, the paper's page 16 reports 187 unaware; it changed no rule, coding or outcome.

cases.afterwards_en: The first authorized run failed importing SciPy before reading data; the failure record is kept and the frozen code, protocol and estimand were unchanged. The same day a bounded-alternative account followed (now in history): a ceiling on how far target-directed responses can move under unchanged evaluation, its probability part proved in Lean 4.29.1 (27 audited declarations, two modules), not applicable to this archive, which has neither a validated score budget nor paired coverage. A contingent-versus-yoked training comparison with a new recipient was named and remains unrun. No thesis changed.
cases.shows_en: No theorem was bound: a frozen calculation on others' records gave a contrast uncertain around zero, and even a clear one would not tell acquired concern from changed payoff expectations.
cases.shows_zh: 没有绑定任何定理：在别人的记录上，按冻结的算法算出的差值在零附近，说不准；就算差值清楚，也分不出是学来的关心，还是对报酬的预期变了。

cases.case_en: A designed field study of whether university rankings (Rauhvargers 2011's inventory) and China's 2008 provincial GDP growth targets were dropped by their own deciding bodies after findings against them; nothing was downloaded or coded.
cases.case_zh: 一项设计中的实地研究：大学排名（Rauhvargers 2011 的清单）和中国各省2008年的GDP增长目标，在被指失准之后，是否被决定它们的机构自己放弃；没有下载任何记录，也没有编码。

things.thing_en: a university ranking with its own section in Rauhvargers (2011); a province's numerical GDP growth target in its 2008 government work report
the ranked: the institutions a ranking ranks; a province's government and the cadres evaluated against the target, and those appointed or promoted on it
the deciding body: a ranking's editors or board; the standing committee of the provincial Party committee
a finding that the measure fails to track what it claims (for a target, that the figures reported against it were false or unreliable)
a recorded material cost falling on the body or the ranked: fines, lost funding, liability, sanctions
an actor outside the ranked who gains a vote, legal authority or a funding condition over the rule (a regulator, a funder, a ministry)

bridges.name: T7's premise, read on a case
bridges.claim_en: A ranking or target is taken as a measure whose rule and reading were documented in advance as set by those it ranks.
bridges.why_en: No record was read. The design's own expectation (AI, from memory, not checked) was that most rankings would code 'premise not met', a publisher's staff setting the rule, and that many provinces would meet the premise by both deciding coders.

bridges.name: absence
bridges.claim_en: Silence in a whole record covering the period is taken as the finding that no new reader arrived, nothing changed in what the ranking reads and no loss entered the selectors' share.
bridges.why_en: It could not be fixed in advance: a coder can report what the documents show, not what the record lacks; the rules for coding absence and for what coders read needed further rules at every one of eleven reader rounds, each finding faults in them.

bridges.name: drift condition
bridges.claim_en: The deciding body's members, their kinds and its voting threshold are taken as the drawn model's selectors, their number and their share's distance from the critical mass (one member drawn at a time, constant readings and cost).
bridges.why_en: No reading of it was made on any record; the readings tried from voting thresholds and from turnover were faulted by the readers; the last needs every replacement over ten years by kind, and in simulation seldom reads 'rare' even where the lock holds. A holding limit from 5 November 2026.

bridges.name: law to prediction: the bound for a drop
bridges.claim_en: DrawnReplacement.lost_above, stated for losing every shaper, is taken to bound a measure's drop, the count passing below the critical mass.
bridges.why_en: The design says the birth-death argument for this is not checked in Lean; its dry run checks it exactly on four chains, where the exact chance is from about two thirds to a twentieth of the bound.

bridges.name: positive controls
bridges.claim_en: LIBOR's cessation and the 2010 abolition of the UK's 2007 Public Service Agreements are taken as cases whose known exits the coding must find before any refutation counts.
bridges.why_en: The controls guard the absence findings and are coded by the same rules, so they share their faults; their exits are from the author's memory, not checked.

bridges.name: a reader outside the share
bridges.claim_en: An actor who gains a place from which the rule is formed or used is taken as a new reader; one who only publishes evidence is not.
bridges.why_en: 02 does not define the phrase; the design says this is its own reading, not the home's, and that the home may need a line fixing it.

predictions.label: the Refuted by (first forbidden case): designed, not frozen
predictions.says_en: No ranking or target meets all eight conditions by both deciding coders: a finding against it, the premise documented in advance, a drop within the window, by its own body, with no new reader, no new reading, no loss entering, and drift rare by the bound (at most 1/20).

ifs.what_en: The premise holds of the case: rule and reading set by those it ranks
The record is shown whole, with a document in every year of each period, so that silence is absence
The drawn model's premises hold of the body and its bound is readable (at least 18 members under a simple majority; every replacement of ten years listed by kind)
Both positive controls show their known exits

predictions.label: the third forbidden case: designed, not frozen
predictions.says_en: No reform that lowers what the measure gives those it favours, made while the reading is still produced by the ranked, still stands after the measure's next regular revision, with no new reader, new reading or loss in between.

ifs.what_en: The premise holds of the case
The record from the reform through the next revision is shown whole and every year covered
Both positive controls show their known exits

predictions.label: the second forbidden case: a reported count, deciding nothing
predictions.says_en: Among cases above the critical mass with their bounds read, those dropped by the body with no exit agreed are no more than independent events at the cases' bounds allow (read as 'more often' where that chance is at most 1/20).

ifs.what_en: The drift bound is readable on enough cases

predictions.label: the controls
predictions.says_en: Each deciding coder codes at least one of the three exits true for LIBOR and for the 2007 Public Service Agreements.

predictions.label: the author's expectation (design section 13; AI, not a prediction of the account)
predictions.says_en: The Refuted by's verdict most likely unresolved or not refuted, refuted below one chance in ten; the third case most likely not testable or unresolved; no case with the drift bound read as rare by both deciders, a provincial standing committee having about a dozen members (from memory).

cases.afterwards_en: Held on 5 November 2026 after eleven reader rounds, every one with a finding of medium severity or higher; the dry run on planted cases grew from 59 checks to 234; the last round's fixes were not read. 02 section 9's Evidence line records the attempt and the drift condition as a holding limit that lapses when a reading of it on a kept record passes a reader round. A smaller test remains possible and unclaimed: one frame, whole records only, three codes, both controls, no drift reading; it could meet the third forbidden case where records fit whole, not the Refuted by. The fourth forbidden case was described, not tested: no known register records who reads a loss. The rounds' branch is kept at refs/salvage/aa7-refuters-2026-11-05.
cases.shows_en: T7's field refuter needs findings of absence and a drift reading; after eleven reader rounds no coding of them could be frozen, and no record was read.
cases.shows_zh: T7 的实地反驳要靠“记录里没有”的判定和一项漂变读数；十一轮审读之后，这套编码还是冻结不了，一份记录也没读。

cases.case_en: Claude Haiku judges list against prose versions of its answers after reading nine answers counted from the loop's earlier picks; planted failed deliveries of lists are noted nowhere, on prose answers, or in a report.
cases.case_zh: Claude Haiku 当评审，在自己答案的列表版和段落版之间挑选，先读九份按循环此前所选比例取出的答案；植入的损失（列表答案投递失败）或无处提及，或只注在段落答案上，或写进报告。

things.thing_en: the counts of list answers and prose answers in the loop's population, from one list to eight prose (Claude Haiku's answers to 24 everyday questions, each in both versions)
Claude Haiku as judge picking the better version in ten pairs; its picks plus one each are the rule, in force from the next step (4 : 1 for lists before the first reading)
the judge's reference set of nine answers 'selected as the best in earlier rounds', counted from the share
failed deliveries of list answers, recorded at five a step (45 by step 8)
a reviewer's note of the failed deliveries on each prose answer in the reference set; the service's delivery report read by the judge

bridges.name: H1-LA2
bridges.claim_en: The judge's reading, formed from its reference set, is taken as a pool of the readers it shows, counted by kind.
bridges.why_en: One note of the loss, on the one prose answer among nine, turned it: prose in all 50 picks of late's first reading in all five seeds, lists in 60 of 60 without the note; the one-note measure is resolved (p = 0.031). The README: H1-LA2 as stated fails for this judge, a pool counted by kind with these readings, not every pool.

bridges.name: H1-LA2, second assertion
bridges.claim_en: Where 8 of 9 readers are list answers, with no note or with one, the judge is taken to favour lists.
bridges.why_en: With no note it chose lists in 60 of 60 picks; with one note it chose prose in all 50.

bridges.name: H1-LA2, third and fourth assertions
bridges.claim_en: Where the readers carrying the loss are the more numerous, or every reader reads it, the judge is taken to favour prose.
bridges.why_en: The frozen first readings: in_time 10 calls, mean share of list picks 0.00, prose (p = 0.001); read_all 5 calls, 0.00, prose (p = 0.031). Post hoc: 0 list picks of 50 at 1 : 8 and at 3 : 6 with notes, and 0 of 50 with the report at each of four counts; wherever a note or the report was in its input the judge chose prose in all 650 picks. At 1 : 8 with no note it chose prose too (3 list picks of 80).

bridges.name: H1-LA2, first assertion
bridges.claim_en: Each list answer is taken to read for lists at least as much as each prose answer does, with or without its note.
bridges.why_en: Not measured apart; the README notes that a pool turned at 8 : 1 by one reading large enough is consistent with it.

bridges.name: T7's premise
bridges.claim_en: This judge is taken as a measure whose rule and reading are formed from what it selected.
bridges.why_en: unread passed, and post hoc, with nothing reading the loss, its picks followed the reference set's counts (0 of 160 with no list answer shown, 150 of 150 with nine). One model reading a set in context; formation by training is untested.

bridges.name: the loop
bridges.claim_en: The counts, the selection, the pace of reading and the planted loss are taken as the model's share, selection, pace and unread growing loss.
bridges.why_en: The loop's arithmetic is the theorems' own, checked against MA2's witness numbers (values.py); the loss is recorded at five a step whatever reads it, and where nothing reads it the judge's input does not depend on it.

bridges.name: the frozen course rule
bridges.claim_en: A share at step 8 not below the share at step 4 is taken as the theorems' 'never below'.
bridges.why_en: The rule reads only the end: late's share returned to its step-4 value exactly at step 8 and was below it at steps 5 and 7, so the course passed without locking.

predictions.label: L1, an unread loss leaves the lock (unread kept)
predictions.says_en: With nothing in the judge's input saying how answers are delivered, the share of list answers at step 8 is not below its share at step 4, while recorded failed deliveries grow.

ifs.what_en: Nothing the judge reads depends on the loss
The loss grows by at least one a step
Selection under a rule favouring lists does not lower their share
At eight lists to one prose with no note, the judge's reading favours lists, agreeing with the rule in force
The judge's reading is a monotone function of the share alone

predictions.seen_en: Kept in 5 of 5 seeds; first reading 5 calls, mean share of list picks 1.00, lists (p = 0.031). Post hoc, held at every step in 5 of 5, the share going from 32/33 at step 4 to 468512/468513 at step 8 while the unread loss grew to 45.
predictions.rival_en: A taste for lists whatever the reference set also keeps this course; it is separated by read_all and in_time turning. 'A single reading suffices' also passes L1.

predictions.label: L2, a loss read by every reader turns the course (read_all turned)
predictions.says_en: With the delivery report read by the judge and the notes on prose answers, from the first reading at step 3, the share of list answers at step 8 is strictly below its share at step 4.

ifs.what_en: The loss grows by at least one a step
Reading the report, the judge favours lists at no count of the reference set

predictions.seen_en: Turned in 5 of 5 seeds; first reading 5 calls, mean share 0.00, prose (p = 0.031). Post hoc, held at every step in 5 of 5, the share going from 32/33 at step 4 to 32/14673 at step 8.
predictions.rival_en: A taste for prose would also turn it (it fails L1); 'a single reading suffices' and 'notes idle' also pass L2.

predictions.label: L3, who reads decides (late kept and read_all turned)
predictions.says_en: The same loss at the same step and counts: noted only on the one prose answer among nine, the share of lists at step 8 is not below step 4; read by the judge in the report, it is strictly below.

ifs.what_en: The judge's reading is a pool of the readers it shows, counted by kind (H1-LA2)
At eight lists to one prose carrying a note, the judge's reading favours lists
The prose answers' reading with the note favours lists no more than the list answers' does
The loss grows by at least one a step

predictions.seen_en: Printed passed. read_all turned in 5 of 5. late counted kept in 5 of 5 by an exact tie, not a lock: its first reading chose prose in all 50 picks (5 calls, mean share 0.00, p = 0.031); from step 4 the share alternated between 32/33 and 32/43, equal at step 8 to step 4 and below it at steps 5 and 7; held at every step in 0 of 5 (post hoc).
predictions.rival_en: The frozen rival 'a single reading suffices'. Post hoc: a threshold reading (lists at or above a share of 17/18, prose below) read one step late alternates and is locked neither way, as the witness RuleCapture.Alternating does; a pool in which one reading of the loss is large enough would read the same.

predictions.label: L4, when it is read decides (in_time turned and late kept)
predictions.says_en: The same notes on prose answers: read from step 0, while prose answers are the more numerous (8 of 9, then 6 of 9), the share of lists at step 8 is strictly below its share at step 2; read from step 3, it is not below its share at step 4.

ifs.what_en: Where the answers carrying the note are the more numerous, the judge favours prose
At eight lists to one prose carrying a note, the judge's reading favours lists
The judge's reading is a pool of the readers it shows, counted by kind (H1-LA2)

predictions.seen_en: Printed passed. in_time turned in 5 of 5 (first reading 10 calls, mean share 0.00, prose, p = 0.001; held at every step in 5 of 5); late kept only by the same tie. The control, with nothing reading the loss, was kept in 1 seed and turned in 4 (first reading 10 calls, mean share 0.43, not resolved).
predictions.rival_en: The counts alone: since the control turned in 4 of 5 seeds, the frozen rules print 'in_time turned by the readers' counts alone, the loss not needed' as supported and 'the loss read in time turned a course that would otherwise be kept' as not supported; the notes measure was resolved (10 paired calls, mean fall 0.43, p = 0.016).

predictions.label: one note in nine (late against unread at step 3; frozen, reported, not counted)
predictions.says_en: Under H1-LA2's second assertion the judge still favours lists with one note among nine; the paired measure asks whether the share of list picks is lower with the note (the power check: resolved with probability 0.01 to 0.03 under H1-LA2's pools, 0.988 under 'a single reading suffices').

ifs.what_en: The paired calls share counts, questions and orders and differ only in the note

predictions.seen_en: Resolved: 5 paired calls, mean fall in the share of list picks 1.00, p = 0.031. With the one note the judge chose prose in all 50 picks; without it, lists in 60 of 60.
predictions.rival_en: This is the frozen rival 'a single reading suffices', the first outcome the predictions file lists under what would change the account.

predictions.label: frozen support rule: 'the counts decide, one note in nine outweighed'
predictions.says_en: Printed as supported where L3 passes and the notes measure (where most readers carry them) is resolved.

ifs.what_en: The rule reads the measures of its own construct (the one-note measure, late's first reading); as frozen it consults neither

predictions.seen_en: Printed supported. The rule consults neither the one-note measure nor late's first reading, and both show the opposite, so the README does not claim it. 'A single reading turned the lock' printed not supported only because its rule needs late to fail, which the tie prevented.

cases.afterwards_en: On 4 November 2026 the per-step record was re-read (T7C; a first draft that found the opposite was reversed by a reader): 02 section 9 and 08's T7 row now say the case occurred at both readings where the loss was read and counts against T7's fourth forbidden case, as worded before its clause on drift (the third in LA2's frozen numbering; the clause was added later and LA2 did not test it), as a claim about trained judges, and against H1-LA2; the pool theorem stands within hypotheses this judge does not meet; T7's other cases are untouched. 08 section 9 took the lesson that a frozen rule fixes how a verdict is scored, not that it reads its construct. late's course is read post hoc as the witness RuleCapture.Alternating.never_locked; no theorem states how such a threshold arises from the readers. The timing theorem's record (ReadInTime, added 26 October 2026) names LA2 as its one frozen test, which found the theorem did not apply. The field test T7F was then designed and held on 5 November 2026.
cases.shows_en: Where nothing read the loss the lock held as the theorem says; the bridge, this judge as a pool counted by kind, failed; two contrasts passed only by a tie.
cases.shows_zh: 没有东西读到损失时，锁定如定理所说保持住了；但“这个评审是按类计数的读者池”这座桥断了，有两项对比只是靠一次平局通过。

cases.case_en: Claude Haiku sets one lineage's policy, shaping its evaluator (S) or not (N), sees only each round's mean score over five rounds, then makes a final choice; six conditions, five seeds each.
cases.case_zh: 让 Claude Haiku 给一个族群定策略：塑造评分者（S），或不塑造（N）。它只看得到每轮的平均分，五轮后做最后选择；六种条件，每种五个种子。

things.thing_en: a lineage whose members shape the evaluator (policy S), each leaving a Poisson number of offspring with mean a + p for m generations, then a + s + p
a lineage whose members do not shape (policy N), each leaving a + c + p
the evaluator's scoring after shaping: s back to the shapers alone (0, 2 or 15), p to every member alike (0, 3 or 5), cost c (1 or 2)
Claude Haiku in context, choosing S or N again after each round and once more at the end
the mean score of a round's 20 runs, the only thing the model sees of its lineage
the model's free-rider framing before any score (27 of 30 seeds chose N in round 0; all 30 first answers speak of free riding)

bridges.name: H1-LA3
bridges.claim_en: Claude Haiku's in-context revision is taken as a selection through the feedback: the policy whose scores read higher is kept.
bridges.why_en: By the frozen measure it holds in s2p3, s0p5 and s0p0 and is low in s2p0, m2n1_p0 and m2n1_p5 (fewer than 4 of 5 seeds played both policies and ended on the better seen). Post hoc, all 21 seeds that played both ended on the higher mean seen and the 9 that played one kept N; the frozen bridge counts both as one measure, so it does not separate them. The binding marks this bridge, not a theorem.

bridges.name: the game as MA3's rule (premise ruleshaping-shaped)
bridges.claim_en: The game's offspring means are taken as the law's rule after shaping: a + s + p for a shaper, a + c + p for an other, with a = 1 and c 1 or 2.
bridges.why_en: game.py sets these means; values.py reproduces the numbers of MA3's witnesses Split, SharedFlips and Timing with the same arithmetic.

bridges.name: counts multiplied, not drawn (premise rulecapture-carriercounts-select)
bridges.claim_en: The lineage's drawn offspring are taken as the law's multiplied counts.
bridges.why_en: The binding assesses it failed of the lineage the agent sees (a branching process with Poisson offspring, means of sampled runs) and holding of the expected scores the frozen predictions read. In the power check, in every condition, all 9,000,000 simulated pairs of one S round and one N round fell in the predicted order. The binding says this premise does not carry the mark.

bridges.name: expected scores as the share's class
bridges.claim_en: The policy with the higher expected score is taken as the kind whose share the theorems on counts say rises.
bridges.why_en: S's and N's expected scores are 100 times the two sides of stretch_iff's inequality; with m = 0 the three-step class equals favours_iff's one-step class by elementary arithmetic, which the predictions file says is not a Lean statement and values.py checks for these numbers.

predictions.label: K1
predictions.says_en: The same total kept or shared: the model ends on shaping (S) in s2p3, where two of five come back to the shapers alone, and on not shaping (N) in s0p5, where all five go to every member; each in at least 4 of 5 seeds.

ifs.what_en: the game's offspring means are the law's rule after shaping, with a = 1 and a cost of 1
the counts are multiplied, not drawn: the game draws Poisson offspring and the agent sees means of 20 sampled runs; it holds of the expected scores the frozen predictions read
H1-LA3 in both conditions: at least 4 of 5 seeds played both policies and ended on the better seen

predictions.seen_en: s2p3: S S S S S; s0p5: N N N N N. Both conditions passed, so K1 passed. H1-LA3 holds in both (5 of 5 played both and ended on the better seen; 4 of 4, with one seed that played N only).
predictions.rival_en: Neither frozen rival gives this pair: the prior account predicts the same final choice in both conditions, the level account S in both. The predictions file adds that a pass does not show the agent reads which part of a return is kept and which is shared: it sees only its totals.

predictions.label: K2
predictions.says_en: What comes back to the shapers alone covers the cost, whatever is shared: S in s2p0 (nothing shared) and in s2p3 (three shared), each in at least 4 of 5 seeds.

ifs.what_en: the game's offspring means are the law's rule after shaping, with a = 1 and a cost of 1
the counts are multiplied, not drawn (holds of the expected scores, fails of the drawn lineage the agent sees)
H1-LA3 in both conditions: holds in s2p3; low in s2p0, where 2 seeds played both policies and 3 played N only

predictions.seen_en: s2p3: S S S S S (passed). s2p0: N N S N S, 2 of 5 on S (failed), so K2 failed. The three s2p0 seeds that ended on N never played S, in a condition where S's expected score is 2,700 against 800.
predictions.rival_en: The model's prior: every s2p0 seed chose N before any score, and a policy never played gives no score; the run does not say why S was tried in some seeds and not others. Neither frozen rival fits the run: final choices differ between conditions, and shaping was dropped where it grew the lineage.

predictions.label: K3
predictions.says_en: Nothing comes back to the shapers alone and shaping has a cost, whatever is shared: N in s0p0 and in s0p5, each in at least 4 of 5 seeds.

ifs.what_en: the game's offspring means are the law's rule after shaping, with a = 1 and a cost of 1 above zero, as nothing_back_falls needs
the counts are multiplied, not drawn (holds of the expected scores, fails of the drawn lineage the agent sees)
H1-LA3 in both conditions: at least 4 of 5 seeds played both policies and ended on the better seen

predictions.seen_en: s0p0: N N N N N; s0p5: N N N N N. Both passed, so K3 passed. H1-LA3 holds in both (4 of 4 that played both; one seed in each played N only).
predictions.rival_en: A prior of N always passes K3 (the power table: it passes K3 only), and 27 of 30 seeds chose N before any score. Post hoc, the free-rider argument the model gives is nothing_back_falls applied before any score, also where something does come back.

predictions.label: K4
predictions.says_en: Across a stretch (two generations before anything comes back, one with it; 15 back to the shapers alone, cost 2) the shared part turns the verdict: N with nothing shared (m2n1_p0), S with five shared (m2n1_p5), each in at least 4 of 5 seeds.

ifs.what_en: the game's offspring means are the law's rule across the stretch, with a = 1 and a cost of 2; the pair is chosen for large differences, not the Lean witness SharedFlips
the counts are multiplied, not drawn (holds of the expected scores, fails of the drawn lineage the agent sees)
H1-LA3 in both conditions: low in both (3 of 3 that played both ended on the better seen; 2 seeds in each played one policy only)

predictions.seen_en: m2n1_p0: N N N N N (passed). m2n1_p5: S S N N S, 3 of 5 on S (failed), so K4 failed. The two m2n1_p5 seeds that ended on N never played S, where S's expected score is 75,600 against 51,200.
predictions.rival_en: The model's prior: the two m2n1_p5 seeds that ended on N chose N before any score and never played S, and a policy never played gives no score; in m2n1_p0, which passed, two seeds also played N only. The run does not say why S was tried in some seeds and not others. Neither frozen rival fits the run: final choices differ between conditions, and shaping was dropped in m2n1_p0, where it grew the lineage.

cases.afterwards_en: 07 records the test beside the D68 readings on shaping: by the frozen reading of one failure, which the README extends to the other, the theorem stands and its reading for trained systems is not supported by this case. LA3's faults entered experiments/README's 'Freezing a test on a trained system': simulate the system the test may meet (this agent never tried the other policy in 9 of 30 seeds), and measure exploration apart from selection (LA3's bridge counted both in one measure, a point a reviewer had named before the freeze).
cases.shows_en: Post hoc, where the model had scored both policies it ended on the better; where it never tried shaping its prior chose: the misses mark the bridge, not the theorem.
cases.shows_zh: 事后看：两种策略都试过的，模型都选了得分高的；从没试过塑造的，就照原先的想法选。落空的是桥，不是定理。

cases.case_en: A stipulated system of three material units and a reserve of energy packets is run for a fixed time with catalyst Y's recycling coefficient at zero or four; eight joint outcomes' probabilities are computed.
cases.case_zh: 一个设定出来的小体系：三份物质，一池能量包。把催化物 Y 的回收系数设为 0 或 4，运行固定的一段时间，算出八种联合结果各自的概率。

things.thing_en: the reserve of usable-energy packets F
capture from the incident source into the reserve, at a rate set by the resident structure C
the two recycling channels (catalysed by C and by Y), each spending one packet to turn degraded material D back into R
the active material R + C + Y, which must not all be degraded by the horizon
the three material units passing among R, C, Y and degraded D by assembly, wear and recycling

bridges.name: physical identification
bridges.claim_en: The declared event law is taken as a physical mechanism with real catalysts and rates.
bridges.why_en: The protocol leaves physical catalyst identification, construction costs, a broader protocol class and the formation or selection of theta as separate obligations; the README calls it a calculation for a stipulated model, not an empirical study.

bridges.name: the parameter intervention
bridges.claim_en: Raising the coefficient from 0 to 4 is taken as a comparison of two supplied preparations.
bridges.why_en: A model-level intervention, with no claim that converting between two physical catalysts is free or available; not a construction theorem.

bridges.name: the fixed run as the capability
bridges.claim_en: Running the installed process for the horizon is taken as what the arrangement reliably delivers.
bridges.why_en: The reliable set is exact for this singleton protocol class and only an inner bound for a larger class of controllers; a failed fixed-run profile does not establish impossibility under all realizable interventions.

bridges.name: the implementation as the declared generator
bridges.claim_en: certify.py's finite chain with a marked overflow state is taken as the declared countable-state process.
bridges.why_en: An independent checker rebuilds the generator without importing the producer, agrees on all 48 probabilities to within 2.78e-15 under a disclosed 1e-11 tolerance, and checks exact integer accounting across 1,000 physical states; its floating calculation is a cross-check, the enclosure resting on the directed-arithmetic argument.

bridges.name: ample-support operation
bridges.claim_en: This weakly driven specimen is taken as standing for sustained operation under ample support.
bridges.why_en: With the fixed source g = 1 the reduced work-equivalent drift is -F-Y, so the README says the specimen does not test ample-support persistent operation; the alpha = 0.5 crossing is specific to the declared source and horizons.

predictions.label: short-time signs (protocol, before the numbers)
predictions.says_en: With lambda = 1 + theta, the chance of at least one recycling event is lambda H + O(H^2) and the chance a reserve packet remains is 1 - (2 + theta)H + O(H^2): raising theta raises one and lowers the other.

ifs.what_en: the declared event law with unit parameters, N = 3 and initial counts (R,C,Y,D,F) = (0,1,1,1,1)

predictions.seen_en: At H = 0.25: at least one recycling event 0.210619412 at coefficient 0 against 0.659720172 at 4; at least one reserve packet left 0.646107828 against 0.344331591. The independent review's exact generator derivatives at the start are 1 + theta and -(2 + theta). Expansion and computed values come from the same declared generator.

predictions.label: joint recycling and assembly
predictions.says_en: The chance that recycling and resident assembly both occur is lambda H^2/2 + O(H^3): higher with the larger coefficient.

ifs.what_en: the declared event law with unit parameters, N = 3 and initial counts (R,C,Y,D,F) = (0,1,1,1,1)

predictions.seen_en: At H = 0.25: 0.024095030 against 0.086651916; with a packet also remaining, 0.006683438 against 0.021045556. Every assembly-required profile stays below reliability 0.5 at H = 0.25.

predictions.label: crossing at reliability 0.5
predictions.says_en: The whole delivery vector is not universally improved by increasing theta; whether the reliable sets at alpha = 0.5 are incomparable needs certified crossings, which the expansions alone do not give, a profile counting only if its interval lies wholly on one side of alpha.

ifs.what_en: the declared event law with unit parameters, N = 3 and initial counts (R,C,Y,D,F) = (0,1,1,1,1)
energy overflow and the omitted Poisson mass stay inside the reported intervals (maximum overflow bound below 1.7e-17; omitted mass at most 1e-22 in each case)

predictions.seen_en: At H = 0.25 the reliable sets are {(0,0,0),(0,0,1)} at coefficient 0 and {(0,0,0),(1,0,0)} at 4, neither containing the other: the first two rows of the README's table cross the common threshold in opposite directions. All declared horizons and all eight profiles are reported.

cases.afterwards_en: Later developments were added in sub-folders, each with its own protocol, law and evidence scope (paid allocation, delivered continuation, turnover paths, a constructed-regulation comparison whose negative outcomes are kept separately, full entry, a complete first successor). The README says the earlier protocol and interval results are unchanged and that no new physical experiment was performed.
cases.shows_en: A model checked against its own expansion: the calculation agrees with the reasoning it came from, and no bridge to an actual system was tried.
cases.shows_zh: 这是模型同它自己的展开式对账：算出来的和推出来的一致；通向实际体系的桥没有试。

cases.case_en: Six forecasters, given an agent's reference course and a lawn cell's own dynamics, forecast which cells die in five thin-margin variants, for an exact best response and 20 tabular learners; Box is measured too.
cases.case_zh: 六种预报法各拿到一个行动者在参考变体里的路线和目标草格自身的动态，预报五种余量很薄的变体里哪些草格会死：对精确最优策略，也对 20 个表格学习者；另外测了推箱子环境。

things.thing_en: a lawn cell with its level (start level, cap 3, gate at 0)
the cell's regrowth, with its period r
the exact best response, and the 20 tabular learner seeds, entering the cell
the task reward, which does not read the lawn
the six forecasters: reference outcome, MQ1's margin band, unreachability of the alive set, relative reachability (undiscounted and discounted), attainable utility
the cell's death, or any lost level, on the target variant's own course

bridges.name: B3 (MQ1's transfer)
bridges.claim_en: The exact best response's course in a thin-margin variant is taken as its course in the reference variant V0.
bridges.why_en: The reward and the dynamics it reads do not read the lawn (pi*-irrelevance, Li, Walsh and Littman 2006); MQ1's B3 passed for the best response. R1: all 10 best-response cells forecast right with the exact death step. The README notes that, ground truth being the target's own course, every replay forecast is then exact by construction.

bridges.name: H2 (MQ1)
bridges.claim_en: The tabular learners are taken as coming near the best return, so that a learner's course in a thin variant is its own reference course.
bridges.why_en: MQ1: the learners fell short of the optimum (5-7.75 deliveries against 9) and its B3 failed for them. Here exact replay is right on 122/200 rows (61%), where the reference outcome, no death, is right on 120/200 (60%); all 78 of replay's errors forecast a death that does not happen, for a learner that drew less in the thin variant. The transfer fails for every forecaster at once.

bridges.name: the margin band as reachability
