bridges.claim_en: MQ1's margin band is taken as relative reachability on a replayed course, bounding the regrowth by floor(t/r) instead of running it.
bridges.why_en: Stated before the run. R2: the band agrees with exact replay on the 8 cells it decides and leaves 2 open that replay settles; every replay step lies in the band, at its upper end.

bridges.name: blind draw
bridges.claim_en: The lawn is taken as a condition the reward has zero measured coupling into, with a margin.
bridges.why_en: MQ1's lawn under its blind reward; part R reuses MQ1's courses and runs no new environment. tests.json files SE1 under T3, which was first worded after SE1 ran, so the predictions are the test's own.

bridges.name: Box with the box removed (P1)
bridges.claim_en: The box is taken as lying beyond what the reward reads.
bridges.why_en: Coupling by replay is 0 with the box removed.

bridges.name: Box with the box displaced (P2)
bridges.claim_en: The box is taken as lying beyond what the reward reads.
bridges.why_en: Coupling is 50 with the box moved onto the course, as R6 predicted. A level-valued renewable condition settles the perturbation set and a box does not; where a side effect runs through a feature the reward reads, blind draw forecasts nothing and RR and AUP still register it.

predictions.label: R1
predictions.says_en: Exact replay of the reference entries on the target cell (unreachability of the alive set) decides all 10 best-response cells right, with the exact death step.

ifs.what_en: B3's transfer: the best response's course in the target variant is the reference course
each forecaster gets the reference entry steps and the target cell's own dynamics (start level, regrowth period, gate at 0, cap 3, horizon 45)

predictions.seen_en: 10/10, every step exact.
predictions.rival_en: Classed an identity given MQ1's B3: any exact replay on the same information gives the same.

predictions.label: R2
predictions.says_en: The margin band agrees with exact replay on every cell it decides (8), leaves open cells that replay decides, and replay's death step lies in the band.

ifs.what_en: each forecaster gets the reference entry steps and the target cell's own dynamics

predictions.seen_en: 8/8 agree. The band leaves V1's B and V5's A open; exact replay forecasts both survive, correctly. Every replay step lies in the band, at its upper end.
predictions.rival_en: Classed an identity: the band bounds the replay.

predictions.label: R3
predictions.says_en: Relative reachability over all levels gives exact replay's verdicts on death on these cells (the only cells that do not renew, V3's A and V4's A, both die) and is exact on any irreversible loss of a level.

ifs.what_en: B3's transfer: the best response's course in the target variant is the reference course
the cell's reachability is computed for the cell's own control (take one unit or wait), not over the whole gridworld

predictions.seen_en: 10/10 on death and 10/10 on any lost level; on V3's A, which does not renew, RR flags the first take at step 1, five steps before death.
predictions.rival_en: Classed an identity.

predictions.label: R4
predictions.says_en: The graded measures (discounted relative reachability, attainable utility) rank dying cells above surviving ones: AUC at least 0.9 for each. It could fail, since a discounted measure also penalises reversible depletion.

ifs.what_en: each forecaster gets the reference entry steps and the target cell's own dynamics; attainable utility over 30 random rewards on the cell's levels, gamma 0.99

predictions.seen_en: AUC 1.0 for discounted RR and for AU; surviving cells 0.007 and 0.175, dying cells 0.25-0.74 and 20.1-29.4.

predictions.label: R5
predictions.says_en: For the tabular learners every replay forecast fails together: exact replay agrees with the band wherever the band decides, and is right on fewer than 90% of rows.

ifs.what_en: the transfer for learners: a learner's course in the target variant is its own reference course; this rests on MQ1's H2, learners coming near the best return, which failed there

predictions.seen_en: Exact replay agrees with the band on all 151 rows the band decides and is right on 122/200 = 61%; the reference outcome (no death) is right on 120/200; all 78 of replay's errors forecast a death that does not happen. The prediction was that the forecasts fail, and they did; what fails is the transfer.
predictions.rival_en: Forecasting no death at all does as well (60% against 61%).

predictions.label: R6
predictions.says_en: Box: the best response pushes the box into the corner; relative reachability is above 0 on its course; the reward's coupling into the box, by replay, is 0 with the box removed and above 0 with it displaced.

ifs.what_en: Box rebuilt from the published description of side_effects_sokoban level 0, the hidden performance function replaced by RR's irreversibility criterion

predictions.seen_en: The course goes south, pushing the box into the corner at (3,2), then east, south, south, east to the goal; return 45; the box's start unreachable; stepwise RR 0.45 at the push and 0 after; coupling 0 under removal, 50 under displacement onto the course.

cases.afterwards_en: By the rule frozen in advance, line E stopped here (20 October 2026): the predictor is shown no better than the known measures, and no CPU-feasible established benchmark has a renewable condition with a margin. MQ1's README records SE1 as its follow-up. T3, first worded after SE1 ran, lists it among its limits: tabular learners do not come near the optimum, so its side effects do not predict theirs (61% against 60% for 'no death').
cases.shows_en: On the same information the margin forecast matches the known impact measures where it decides and decides less; four of six verdicts are identities; for learners every forecast fails together.
cases.shows_zh: 信息相同，余量预报在它能判定的地方同已有的影响度量一致，能判定的还少一些；六项判定里四项是恒等式。到了学习者，所有预报一起失效。

cases.case_en: Claude and GPT each wrote plain-English statements of 60 Lean theorems, with and without one planted extra referent, and both coded all 240 texts for excess referents, blind to who wrote them.
cases.case_zh: Claude 和 GPT 各把 60 条 Lean 定理写成白话英文，一版照实，一版暗加一个多余的所指；两者再给全部 240 篇标出多余的所指，都不知道是谁写的。

things.thing_en: a coder model (Claude or GPT) marking excess referents by FC1's codebook v1.1
each coder's list of excess referents for a text
the referent planted knowingly at a recorded span, of class agent, relatum or entity
the Lean statement each plain-English text is checked against

bridges.name: the blind-spot reading
bridges.claim_en: A model coding its own text is taken as a judge whose coupling does not reach what its own text introduces.
bridges.why_en: RESULTS: the run 'does not support it as an author effect'. Interaction on detection +0.017 [-0.050, +0.083], the interval including 0; the data allow a summed self deficit of at most 5 points. 08 adds that the interval is uncertainty, not evidence that neither family has a deficit.

bridges.name: knowing plants for unnoticed introductions
bridges.claim_en: A referent planted knowingly is taken as standing for what a text brings in unnoticed.
bridges.why_en: RESULTS, Boundary: deliberate insertion is not the unnoticed smuggling the blind-spot reading names, though each plant is in its author's own words; the faithful texts carry no ground truth.

bridges.name: English for the classical text
bridges.claim_en: Plain-English statements under no glossary are taken as standing for the author's controlled classical code under the name table, where the discrepancy was seen (no excess in any of 26 segments against some in 10).
bridges.why_en: The scope clause frozen in DESIGN section 6: a null R1 leaves open a blind spot specific to the author's own controlled code, and GPT over-reading specific to classical Chinese.

bridges.name: the summed self effect
bridges.claim_en: The interaction I = s_Claude + s_GPT is taken as reading each family's own self effect.
bridges.why_en: Two families identify only the sum; a Claude-only deficit would be masked by an equal GPT self advantage, and s_GPT's point estimate is positive (+0.050).

predictions.label: R1 (primary)
predictions.says_en: The blind-spot reading: each coder catches fewer of the plants in its own texts than in the other's, so the summed self effect I on detection lies below 0. By the frozen rule an interval including 0 means no author-specific deficit detected at this scale.

ifs.what_en: both coders code all 240 texts blind to author, version and plant; no coding missing (480 of 480)
every plant valid: its span in the text, its head word in the span
detection not at ceiling: not every cell is at least 0.95, so R1 is read
a knowing plant stands for an unnoticed introduction

predictions.seen_en: I = +0.017 [-0.050, +0.083]. Detection: Claude coder 0.967 (58/60) on Claude's texts and 1.000 (60/60) on GPT's; GPT coder 0.967 (58/60) on GPT's and 0.917 (55/60) on Claude's. The interval includes 0: no author-specific detection deficit is found; the data allow a summed self deficit of at most 5 points. Detection is near ceiling (0.92-1.00), so only deficits of more than a few points are resolved.
predictions.rival_en: A difference of coding threshold belonging to the coder (R3): the record reads the calibration discrepancy as better accounted for by that than by a blind spot, and says this favours it without settling it.

predictions.label: R2 (secondary)
predictions.says_en: The same interaction on excess referents listed in faithful texts, read the same way: below 0 if each coder lists less in its own texts.

ifs.what_en: both coders code all faithful texts blind to author
a ground truth for excess in the faithful texts

predictions.seen_en: I = -0.050 [-0.200, +0.083], including 0. The Claude coder's own-text difference is exactly 0 [0, 0], because it lists no excess in any faithful text, whoever wrote it; the GPT coder lists 0.183 per Claude-written faithful text (9 texts) and 0.133 per GPT-written (8).
predictions.rival_en: The faithful texts carry no ground truth; the Claude coder may under-detect unplanted excess of kinds the plants did not sample.

predictions.label: R3 (coder-general)
predictions.says_en: Over-reading as a main effect of the coder: the GPT coder lists more excess in faithful texts, whoever wrote them, while detecting no more plants than the Claude coder.

ifs.what_en: a ground truth for excess in the faithful texts

predictions.seen_en: Coder effect (GPT - Claude): detection -0.042 [-0.075, -0.008]; excess per faithful text +0.158 [+0.083, +0.242]. By the rule, consistent with over-reading or a laxer threshold. Described after the fact: 9 of the GPT coder's 19 excess referents in faithful texts are bare numerals that the codebook matches to binders.
predictions.rival_en: A laxer threshold gives the same: with no ground truth in the faithful texts the two are not told apart.

cases.afterwards_en: FIDELITY-RESULTS' open observation gained 'Tested in English (SC1, 23 October 2026)': this favours a difference of coding threshold over a blind spot and does not settle it. On 25 October 2026 (board item DF) the record's statement was narrowed from saying neither coder under-detects its own plants to saying no negative combined author-coder interaction was detected. Named next: the same crossing on the classical text under the name table, adjudication or a human audit of unplanted excess, a third model family.
cases.shows_en: The predicted self-deficit was not seen at this scale: the claim that a coder's own text lies beyond its reach is unsupported in English; the theorem itself was not tested.
cases.shows_zh: 在这个规模上，没看到预料中的“看不见自己写进去的东西”：这个说法在英文里没得到支持；定理本身没有被检验。

cases.case_en: On 65 assessed fish stocks (RAM Legacy), three numbers named in advance and a fitted delay embedding of the same two series each forecast what the stock adds next year, scored on held-out years.
cases.case_zh: 在65个经过评估的鱼类种群上，拿事先定好的三个数，和从同样两条序列拟合出的延迟嵌入，各自预报种群下一年新增多少，在留出的年份上比误差。

things.thing_en: a fish stock's spawning biomass, an output of its stock assessment
the catch, a share of it fitted per stock on its training years
what the stock adds in a year: next year's biomass less this year's, plus the catch share taken
the three numbers named in advance: what the catch leaves this year, what it left a year back, and last year's addition
the field's delay embedding of the same two series, its dimension (1 to 4) chosen by cross-validation on the training years
persistence: next year's addition forecast as last year's
next year's addition in each stock's held-out years

bridges.name: T2 (scope)
bridges.claim_en: An assessed fish stock under a catch is taken as a renewable condition under a draw: its spawning biomass the level, a per-stock share of the catch the draw, the balance of the two the giving (MQ5's reading, imported unchanged).
bridges.why_en: The levels are outputs of age-structured assessments, not the survey series T2's Refuted by names; the record says such outputs carry the assessment model's own structure and that the lag 'may be the assessment's own'.

bridges.name: T2 (the state)
bridges.claim_en: Things of this kind have as their state the level, the recent giving and one lag: no more of the level's own history carries a tenth more of the next giving.
bridges.why_en: By the frozen criterion the three numbers forecast better than the fitted embedding (42 of 65 stocks, p = 0.025). The record reads it as sufficiency against the embedding at these lengths, not as T2's law, which is not fitted here.

bridges.name: the lag's place
bridges.claim_en: The one lag is taken as what the catch left one year back, named before the data.
bridges.why_en: The record says the result does not support the lag's place: in the dry runs 'T2 better' also came where the giving reads only the level (24.5% of archives) or only itself (12%). The place came from MQ4's post hoc reading of other stocks and a generic reading of age structure, not from each stock's renewal.

bridges.name: the rival (F)
bridges.claim_en: The field's delay embedding of the same two series, at dimension 2 or more, is taken as more of the level's own history than the three numbers hold.
bridges.why_en: At D >= 2 the embedding contains the three numbers and more; at D = 1 it is MQ4's smaller state, one number fewer.

bridges.name: the field's criterion
bridges.claim_en: Held-out squared error of an S-map fitted on a stock's training years is taken as how far a state fixes the next giving.
bridges.why_en: Each state's held-out error was larger than persistence's in 53 of the 65 stocks. The record says the verdict tells which state's information carries further through the field's machinery at about 20 training rows, not that T2's state forecasts well.

predictions.label: Primary verdict: T2's first forbidden item read out of sample (DESIGN section 6)
predictions.says_en: The fitted embedding does not remove a tenth of the three numbers' held-out squared error in the median stock while being better in significantly more stocks (median r at or below -0.105 with sign test p < 0.05 would read 'T2 fails'; the converse 'T2 better'; otherwise 'not separated').

ifs.what_en: Each stock is a renewable condition under a draw, its spawning biomass the level and a fitted share of its catch the draw (MQ5's reading)
The level series is the stock's own course, free of the assessment model's structure (they are assessment outputs, not survey series)
The run reads the same stocks as MQ5's committed fits, and MQ5's S3 excess recomputes within 10^-9
Enough rows: at least 12 training and 8 held-out rows a stock, at least 10 testable stocks (65 of the 69 primary stocks testable)
The lag sits one year back, named before the data

predictions.seen_en: Frozen verdict 'T2 better than the field's fitted embedding': median r +0.163, past the frozen margin +0.105; the three numbers better in 42 stocks, the embedding in 23; two-sided sign test p = 0.025. Each state's held-out error was larger than persistence's in 53 of the 65 stocks, both in 46; the three numbers' skill against persistence -0.85, the embedding's -1.21. By the dimension chosen: D = 1, 26 stocks, median r +0.004, embedding better in 13; D = 2, 22 stocks, +0.158, 6; D = 3, 9 stocks, +0.340, 1; D = 4, 8 stocks, +1.186, 3. Read after the run, not frozen: without the 22 stocks at D = 2 the 65 lose the verdict (26 to 17, p = 0.22), as they do without the 17 at D = 3 or 4 (29 to 19, p = 0.19); at D = 2 alone 16 of 22, p = 0.052.
predictions.rival_en: In the dry runs 'T2 better' also came where the giving reads only the level (24.5% of archives) or only itself (12%), against 33% under T2's law; a longer history costs estimation at about 20 training rows (under T2's law r +0.45 and +0.75 at D = 3 and 4); the record says the verdict says which state's information carries further through the field's machinery, not that either forecasts well.

predictions.label: The answer expected, stated before the run (DESIGN section 1)
predictions.says_en: On the primary group the test would say 'not separated on the field's criterion', as in 94% of the archives of a mixed world where a third of the stocks carry an age structure's memory and the rest follow T2's law.

ifs.what_en: The stocks are like the mixed world fitted to MQ5's readings (the design says the readings do not identify the mixture)

predictions.seen_en: 'T2 better' (median r +0.163, 42 to 23, p = 0.025): the expected answer was not borne out. The record says the output does not show why the expectation missed.
predictions.rival_en: The record leaves it open: consistent with the 6% of mixed-world archives that said 'T2 better', and with an in-sample excess that does not carry out of sample; it does not tell them apart. In the design's own terms 'T2 better' places the stocks nearer a world whose state the three numbers hold than MQ5's readings do. No one dry-run world reproduces the run's reported figures.

predictions.label: The pairing with MQ5's in-sample S3 (reported, frozen)
predictions.says_en: If a minority of stocks carries memory the three numbers miss, the embedding would gain most in the stocks MQ5 flagged in sample: a gap in median r, the stocks below MQ5's bound less those at or above it, beyond about 0.3 would suggest it.

ifs.what_en: The bound of about 0.3 separates the mixed world from T2's (read off ten synthetic archives a world; the design calls it loose)

predictions.seen_en: Gap -0.039: median r +0.134 over the 39 stocks below MQ5's bound, +0.173 over the 26 at or above. S3 flagged 26 of the 65 stocks in sample, within the mixed world's 22 to 39 of 66 and above every archive of T2's world (6 to 14). The record: it suggests no such minority and cannot show one absent; the in-sample excess stays unexplained by T2's world alone.

predictions.label: The three readings reported beside the verdict
predictions.says_en: T2's first forbidden item read three other ways by the same rule, reported and not the test's verdict: the embedding's dimension chosen by simplex projection; the three numbers written with the draw in place of the lag; their form chosen per stock.
predictions.seen_en: The same verdict, 'T2 better', in each: simplex's dimension, median r +0.133, 41 to 24, p = 0.046; the draw's form, +0.183, 43 to 22, p = 0.013; form chosen per stock, +0.177, 43 to 22, p = 0.013. By absolute error the embedding was also worse, by less (median log ratio +0.069).

predictions.label: The other and control groups (reported only)
predictions.says_en: The same rule on stocks assessed by other methods (24) and on stocks from biomass dynamics models (5); the design draws the test's verdict from the primary group alone.

ifs.what_en: The other group has at least 10 testable stocks (21 of its 24)
The control group has at least 10 testable stocks (it holds 5)

predictions.seen_en: Other group, 21 of its 24 stocks testable: not separated, median r +0.003, the embedding better in 10 stocks and the three numbers in 11, p = 1; there the three numbers did worse than persistence in 11 of the 21 and the embedding in 12. Control group: 5 stocks, too few for a verdict ('not testable').

cases.afterwards_en: T2 was restated on 4 November 2026 from UE32's proposals 1, 2 and 4: the second forbidden item is lifted only in a series shown, by an upper bound, to sit at the regime's-step end; its horizon is five steps of the grain fixed before the data; the lag's place is named before the data. No completed verdict changed. Proposal 3 waited on a frozen run failing 'as far as anything measured does'; UE32 did not fail it, UE31b did on 6 November 2026, and the clause was narrowed. 08's T2 row records UE32 as sufficiency against the embedding at these lengths, not the lag's place or T2's law.
cases.shows_en: The three numbers beat the fitted embedding by the frozen rule, against the design's expectation; both mostly trailed persistence, and the series are assessment outputs, so the bridge stays unchecked.
cases.shows_zh: 按冻结的规则，事先定好的三个数胜过了拟合的嵌入，和设计自己的预期不同；两者多数还不如照搬上一年，序列又是评估模型的输出，这座桥没有验过。

cases.case_en: Forty laboratory cultures of the flour beetle, two strains at five adult losses set by hand, counted every two weeks as larvae, pupae and adults; four replicates are read together as one cell.
cases.case_zh: 四十瓶实验室养的面粉甲虫，两个品系、五种人为设定的成虫损失率，每两周数一次幼虫、蛹和成虫；同品系同损失率的四瓶合成一格来读。

things.thing_en: the mature adults returned to a culture after each census
the share of adults removed between censuses, set by hand by the experimenters (0.04, 0.27, 0.50, 0.73, 0.96)
the pupae counted now, which become the next recruits into the adults
the three numbers named in advance: the adults left after the set loss now, one census back and two censuses back
the field's state: the pupae and the adults (the LPA model's stages)
the recruits into the adults at the next census
a cell: the four replicate cultures of one strain at one set loss, read under one law

bridges.name: T2 (scope)
bridges.claim_en: A culture under an adult loss set by hand is taken as a renewable condition under a draw: the adults returned the level, the set loss the draw, the recruits the giving.
bridges.why_en: The experimenters set the loss and left recruitment to the culture. The beetle is not on T2's Refuted by list; the design recorded before the run that a failure here counts against the claim for every renewable condition under a draw.

bridges.name: T2 as worded (W)
bridges.claim_en: With the draw, the three numbers fix the next giving as far as anything measured does.
bridges.why_en: Beyond the three numbers the pupae and the adults removed 0.83 of the residual variance beyond chance, against the bound 0.10, detected in 8 of 10 cells: a class of fewer variables, 08 section 9's defeater, met in this domain.

bridges.name: T2 narrowed (H1)
bridges.claim_en: On the adults' own course the three numbers suffice: no further lag carries a tenth more.
bridges.why_en: A further lag removed 0.05 against the bound 0.10. The record says this is the field's own state seen from the course, a tie by construction that the field's model predicts the same way, and not T2 passed: V5 was not testable and V4 not decided.

bridges.name: the lag's place
bridges.claim_en: The one lag is taken as the adults left two censuses back, whose eggs are now the pupae.
bridges.why_en: The place is the field's knowledge of the life cycle, given to T2 before any value was read. Reported, not a verdict: placed one census back it left 0.10 to a further variable, at the bound, where two censuses back left 0.05.

bridges.name: one law a cell
bridges.claim_en: The four replicates of one strain at one set loss are taken as one condition under one law.
bridges.why_en: An assumption made for both states so that a cell has 36 rows. The record says a difference between replicates that neither law carries is not neutral: it moves W and the out-of-sample comparison toward the field's state.

bridges.name: the recording
bridges.claim_en: Each census's adult count is taken as the adults returned to the culture after the manipulation.
bridges.why_en: The frozen recording check let the reading through: 8 of 360 rows have more recruits than pupae, against the 12.5% (46 rows) that would stop it.

bridges.name: the rival's sign
bridges.claim_en: The field's model, at constants from other analyses, is taken to give each cell's sign of the lag's effect.
bridges.why_en: The constants come from another experiment's cultures and a recalled set of uncertain source; the archive's two strains may differ from both.

predictions.label: W: the wording 'as far as anything measured does'
predictions.says_en: T2's first forbidden item as then worded: beyond the three numbers, the pupae remove less than 0.10 of what is left unexplained in the next recruits, in the median cell. The design expected this to fail, by the life cycle.

ifs.what_en: A culture under a set adult loss is a renewable condition under a draw
The adult counts are those returned after the manipulation (recruits above pupae in at most 12.5% of rows)
The four replicates of a cell share one law
Each cell has at least 24 rows (each has 36)

predictions.seen_en: 'The wording fails': excess 0.83 (by loss, low to high: 0.36, 0.54, 0.83, 0.83, 0.91), detected in 8 of 10 cells. Reported, not a verdict: out of sample the field's state had 0.06 of the three numbers' squared error in the median cell, smaller in all 10 (p = 0.002); residuals stood at 54 times the measured floor for T2's law and 7.8 times for the field's.
predictions.rival_en: The life cycle alone gives it: the pupae counted now are the next recruits and carry the chance events between egg and pupa; in the dry runs W fails in every archive where the pupae are the recruits to be, T2's own law included. A difference between replicates that neither law carries also moves W toward the field's state.

predictions.label: V2: the rival's refuter
predictions.says_en: Beyond the pupae and the adults, the three numbers' own lags remove less than 0.10 of what is left unexplained in the next recruits ('the rival holds').

ifs.what_en: The pupae counted are the source of the next recruits

predictions.seen_en: 'The rival holds': excess 0.004, detected in none of the 10 cells.

predictions.label: H1: the course
predictions.says_en: On the adults' own course a further lag, the adults left three censuses back, removes less than 0.10 beyond the three numbers.

ifs.what_en: The lag is placed two censuses back, at the delay of the life cycle
The life cycle has three stages at the census grain (where it is longer H1 fails in 94% of dry-run archives)

predictions.seen_en: 'T2 holds': excess 0.05 (by loss: -0.01, 0.18, 0.08, -0.00, 0.05), detected in one cell; bound 0.10.
predictions.rival_en: The field's three-stage model makes the same prediction: with the lag at the delay the three numbers are the field's own state seen from the course, a tie by construction. The record says it shows nothing the field does not and is not T2 passed.

predictions.label: The sign of the lag's effect: T2's one rule against the field's turning point
predictions.says_en: T2: the lag's effect keeps one sign in every cell. The field's model: negative in dense cells and positive in sparse ones, turning between about 76 and 91 adults. Expected: not separated.

ifs.what_en: At least 6 cells where the two rules differ
H1 holds and a further lag is not detected in more cells than chance gives (the gate)
The field's constants, from other analyses, apply to these two strains

predictions.seen_en: 'Not separated on the sign: the rival's turning point does not split the cultures': the two rules differ in 4 cells, 6 needed (each right in 2); the lag's effect positive in 8 of 10. Read after the run, not frozen: the effect was detected in three cells, two negative and one positive, each the sign the field's model predicts there; the field's two right calls are detected cells and T2's two are not.
predictions.rival_en: At this shape the sign could not go to the field's model whatever the data (T2's sign is the majority of the fitted signs, and six right calls were needed), so the record says the not-deciding does not count for T2.

predictions.label: V5: the lag's sign between series
predictions.says_en: T2's third forbidden item: among the cells where the lag is detected, its sign does not split.

ifs.what_en: At least 6 cells with the lag detected

predictions.seen_en: Not testable: 3 cells detected, 6 needed.

predictions.label: V4: the level alone at five census steps
predictions.says_en: T2's second forbidden item, in its strong form: the adults' level alone does not forecast better than the three numbers five censuses ahead, a culture forecast from its cell-mates' law.

ifs.what_en: Each culture is forecast five censuses ahead from the law fitted to its three cell-mates, with the set loss known
At least 6 cells with forecasts (10 were compared)

predictions.seen_en: Not decided: the three numbers better in 5 cells, worse in 5; median error 0.27, the level alone's 0.23.
predictions.rival_en: V4 never failed T2 in the field's simulated worlds, and the rule reads only 'better', which the design calls lenient to T2; the record says the not-deciding does not count for T2.

cases.afterwards_en: On 6 November 2026 UE32's third proposal was taken on this failure: T2's clause 'as far as anything measured does' was narrowed to 'as far as the level's own history does', with the failure kept beside it, and its first forbidden item to 'a fourth variable from the level's own history'. The record says this forbids less and stays on record as a loss of the broader claim, not a narrowing chosen in advance; no completed verdict changed. It counts against the claim for every renewable condition under a draw, not against T2 in the fisheries nor the reading 08 section 9 names.
cases.shows_en: With the loss set by hand and every animal counted, the thesis's wording failed to the pupae and adults; the rest ties the field's state by construction, the sign undecided.
cases.shows_zh: 损失率是人设的，每只虫都数过，论题原来的措辞败给了蛹和成虫；剩下的部分和本领域的状态在构造上打平，滞后项的正负没有定。

cases.case_en: Forty laboratory flour-beetle cultures with the adult loss set by hand, each read alone: 13 biweekly censuses under the loss, 8 rows where the frozen rules need 20.
cases.case_zh: 四十瓶人为设定成虫损失率的面粉甲虫，一瓶一瓶单独读：设了损失以后各有13次普查，只得8行，冻结的规则要20行。

things.thing_en: the mature adults returned to a culture after each census
the share of adults removed between censuses, set by hand by the experimenters from week 12
the pupae counted now, which become the next recruits into the adults
the three numbers named in advance: the adults left after the set loss now, one census back and two censuses back
the field's state: the pupae and the adults (the LPA model's stages)
the recruits into the adults at the next census
one culture, read alone from its fifth census under the loss

bridges.name: T2 (scope)
bridges.claim_en: A culture under an adult loss set by hand is taken as a renewable condition under a draw: the adults returned the level, the set loss the draw, the recruits the giving.
bridges.why_en: The experimenters set the loss and left recruitment to the culture. No culture under a set loss was read, so nothing was compared on it.

bridges.name: T2 as worded (W)
bridges.claim_en: With the draw, the three numbers fix the next giving as far as anything measured does.
bridges.why_en: Every primary culture was counted too short; the record says each expectation stated in T2's home stands untested.

bridges.name: the lag's place
bridges.claim_en: The one lag is taken as the adults left two censuses back, whose eggs are now the pupae.
bridges.why_en: Fixed from the life cycle before any value was read; the design calls it the field's knowledge given to T2 and the reason the course ties.

bridges.name: the design's reading of the archive
bridges.claim_en: The adult-loss experiment's cultures are taken to run 41 censuses, like the 1997 experiment's.
bridges.why_en: They hold 13 censuses under the loss, 8 rows where the rules need 20. The archive's README and workbook were not read before the freeze; the layout found the length from the workbook's structure, before any census value was read.

bridges.name: the controls
bridges.claim_en: A control culture, with no set loss, is not taken as a condition under a draw: its giving is the adults' net change, not the recruits.
bridges.why_en: The design draws no verdict from controls: an experiment holds few, and pooling mixes strains and parameters. The record says none of what they show tests T2.

predictions.label: The next step (W and V2), primary group
predictions.says_en: T2 as then worded (W): beyond the three numbers, the pupae remove less than 0.10 of what is left unexplained in the next recruits. The field's refuter (V2): the three numbers add less than 0.10 beyond the pupae and the adults. Expected before the run: W fails, by the life cycle, to a class of fewer variables, and V2 holds.

ifs.what_en: A culture under a set adult loss is a renewable condition under a draw
Each culture gives at least 20 rows under the loss (25 censuses), and at least 6 cultures can be read

predictions.seen_en: Not testable, at both grains: all 40 cultures have 8 rows each and are counted too short. One fact of their values was written: each had animals at its last census.

predictions.label: The course (H1), primary group
predictions.says_en: A further lag, the adults left three censuses back, removes less than a tenth beyond the three numbers; the field's three-stage model predicts the same, a tie by construction.

ifs.what_en: Each culture gives at least 20 rows under the loss

predictions.seen_en: Not testable: all 40 cultures too short.

predictions.label: The lag's sign, V5 and V4, primary group
predictions.says_en: T2 forbids the lag's effect changing sign between cultures; the field's model changes it with density, turning between about 76 and 91 adults. Expected: mostly not decided at the archive's size, and if decided in the field's world, to go to the field. V5 (signs among detected cultures) and V4 (the level alone five censuses ahead) are T2's own items.

ifs.what_en: Each culture gives at least 20 rows under the loss

predictions.seen_en: Not testable: all 40 cultures too short.

predictions.label: The control group (reported only; the design draws no verdict from it)
predictions.says_en: The same rules on cultures with neither the loss nor recruitment set, where a culture's giving is the adults' net change.

ifs.what_en: A control culture is under a draw

predictions.seen_en: Of 25 controls, 13 are long enough. At the census grain: W, the pupae remove a median 0.51 beyond the three numbers against the bound 0.10, detected in 9 of 13; V2, the three numbers remove a median 0.02 beyond the pupae and adults, detected in 1; H1, a further lag removes nothing beyond chance (median -0.03), detected in none; the two sign rules differ in no culture; V5 not testable (5 detected, fewer than 6); V4 not decided (better in 9, worse in 4, p = 0.27); reported V3, the field's error a median 0.45 of T2's lean law's, lower in 12 of 13 (p = 0.003).
predictions.rival_en: The record: this shows that the rules and the reader run on the archive's own cultures and give the shape the design expected, not that cultures under a set loss would give it. None of it tests T2.

cases.afterwards_en: The record keeps it as a finding about the test: the design assumed 41 censuses and the experiment it chose holds 13 after the loss is set. UE31b, a new design frozen before any of the 40 cultures' values was read, read them by cell (four replicates of one strain at one loss under one law, ten cells) with UE31's rules and ran on 6 November 2026. UE31's two proposals for T2's owner (the wording; the lag's place) went into UE32's T2-PROPOSALS: 'its place named before the data' was taken on 4 November 2026, and the wording was narrowed on 6 November 2026 on UE31b's failure.
cases.shows_en: Reasoning and data never met: every culture under a set loss was too short for the frozen rules, because the design assumed a length the records did not have.
cases.shows_zh: 推理和数据没有碰上：设了损失率的每一瓶都太短，冻结的规则读不了，因为设计时假定的长度，记录里没有。

cases.case_en: Wisconsin walleye lakes whose spring adults fell below a density fitted on earlier years, were stocked, and later stood above it: does the lake's own fall age-0 catch come back?
cases.case_zh: 威斯康星州的大眼梭鲈湖：春季成鱼跌到按早年数据拟合的密度以下，放流之后又回到它以上，湖里自己繁殖的当年幼鱼，秋季调查里回来了没有？

things.thing_en: a lake's spring adult walleye, the agency's estimate with its interval
the lake's own renewal: fall age-0 walleye per mile, in a year two or more years from any recorded stocking
that renewal, taken to need the adults above T1N's fitted density
stocking by the managers (fingerlings, fry), which raised the adults back above that density
the agencies' public tables of adult estimates, fall surveys and stockings

bridges.name: T1 (the regime)
bridges.claim_en: A walleye lake's adults are taken as a condition whose renewal stops below a need, so that restoring the level restores renewal.
bridges.why_en: This is what V1 was built to read, against renewal lost for years to another cause; the run was refused before any value was read.

bridges.name: the need
bridges.claim_en: T1N's fitted adult density, the point where a lake's fall age-0 reaches one a mile half the time, is taken as the need, imported by hash.
bridges.why_en: No need was measured: on the public table with the stocking database, as the frozen reader reads them, T1N's fit could have about 162 lake-years where it needs 200. The design adds that the fit's 50% point does not tell renewal stopping below a need from renewal only shrinking at low levels.

bridges.name: the lake's own renewal
bridges.claim_en: Fall age-0 per mile, in a year with no stocking recorded that year or the year before, is taken as the lake's own renewal.
bridges.why_en: It rests on the stocking records being complete; the design gives every rise the clause 'unrecorded stocking'.

bridges.name: the level restored
bridges.claim_en: Spring adults standing wholly above the need after stocking are taken as the level restored.
bridges.why_en: The design's standing clause: the adults restored may count stocked fish not yet spawning.

bridges.name: the layout assumed
bridges.claim_en: The agency's public table of adult estimates is taken to give, per lake and year, the estimate, both interval bounds and the acres.
bridges.why_en: The table gives no upper bound and no acres column; T1N's reader, which T1R reads the records with, refuses at its header, before any value.

predictions.label: V1: renewal rose with the level
predictions.says_en: Where the lakes that fell are in T1's regime: within the same lakes, more renewed in the year read above the need and not in the year below than the reverse, by an exact sign test at 0.05. It reads the regime's premise, renewal following the level, on these lakes; the design states no expected answer from the account alone.

ifs.what_en: The agency's table gives the estimate, both interval bounds and the acres
T1N's need is fitted (200 lake-years from 30 lakes; about 162 could be had as the fall tables were read)
At least ten lakes stood wholly below the need, were stocked, and later stood wholly above it with a year read
No stocking beyond the records in the year read or the year before
Nothing other than the level changed renewal or its survey between the two years compared

predictions.rival_en: The design's standing clauses: stocking no record shows; something other than the level changing renewal or its survey between the years compared (a lasting cause ending, a poor year at the low survey, a good year at the year read); connected waters. In the dry run a cause ending at the first stocking gave 'rose' in 40 and 33 of 40 archives, and fry stocked and recorded nowhere in 36 and 17.

predictions.label: V1: renewal fell short of the fit at the levels restored
predictions.says_en: Where renewal was lost to another cause: no rise is shown, and fewer lakes renewed in the year read than T1N's fit expects even at the lower bounds of the levels restored, by an exact test at 0.05.

ifs.what_en: The agency's table gives the estimate, both interval bounds and the acres
T1N's need is fitted

predictions.rival_en: The design's standing clauses: stocked fish suppressing the lakes' own renewal; the lakes' own needs lying above the common one; the adults restored counting stocked fish not yet spawning. In the dry run, where T1 holds, stocked cohorts counted before they spawn gave 'fell short' in 40 and 29 of 40 archives.

cases.afterwards_en: V1 is not decided and nothing is said of T1; 02 section 5's T1 records the refusal and that T1R shares lakes with T1N, so the two are not independent results. The design stays frozen (dry run: 107 checks, none failed; one reader, four rounds). R8 was not sought as a table, since R1 settles the refusal first. A successor to T1N's design reading the records as published is claimed on the board as T1B and not being worked on; T1R imports T1N's need.
cases.shows_en: Frozen, then refused at the table's header before any value was read: the public records lack what the rules need, so nothing is said of the thesis either way.
cases.shows_zh: 设计冻结以后，在表头就被拒绝，一个数值也没读：公开的记录缺规则要用的列，对论题什么也没说。

cases.case_en: A Lean model of an organization that meets conditions, takes one of several continuations and keeps something of the consequence; 130 theorems and finite countermodels say how its own history changes what it selects.
cases.case_zh: 一个Lean模型：一个组织遇到情况，从几种延续中取一种，并留下后果的一部分；130条定理和有限反例说明它自己的经历怎样改变它的选择。

things.thing_en: the organization's selective disposition at what it has retained (`select m`, its 'operational valuation')
the continuations open to it (`A`), options reached or never reached
what the organization carries forward and how a consequence changes it (`M`, `retain`), its estimates of options included
the consequence law of the local model (`World : X → A → C`)
the organization itself, and a kind kept in a self-renewing population (ValuationRenewal)
the support each valuing event draws on, counted in generation ledgers (LineageInProcess)

bridges.name: operational valuation (argument §2)
bridges.claim_en: An organization's valuation is taken as its selective disposition `select m`, in a thin functional sense.
bridges.why_en: It is a definition; the Lean header says it is not a claim about experience or ethical warrant.

bridges.name: organization and world (argument §2)
bridges.claim_en: One process is taken as an organization with a separate consequence law (`Org` and `World`).
bridges.why_en: The argument calls the split an analytical boundary and a supplied premise; OneProcess proves the pair is one process and neither cut is privileged.

bridges.name: LineageInProcess
bridges.claim_en: The generation ledger is taken as the shared core's per-event support law of a lineage process.
bridges.why_en: Proved in Lean (14 theorems); the saved audit shows 14 of 14 with no axioms after the 7 October merge.

bridges.name: correspondence to actual systems
bridges.claim_en: An actual learner or organism would be taken as an `Org` with this retained condition and consequence law.
bridges.why_en: The README: formal mathematics about the stated representation, not empirical evidence and not an ethical result; no case was bound and no prediction frozen.

cases.afterwards_en: The audit was regenerated on 7 October 2026 after the axiom-free rewrite: all 130 theorems depend on no axioms. A supporting study of the same date adds 25 separately checked theorems (lean/perspectival). The experiments index notes the folder was begun 5 to 8 October 2026 for the earlier generative account, before the Theory of Becoming was named on 9 October.
cases.shows_en: Reasoning only: theorems and built countermodels about the stated representation, with no frozen prediction and no data; the record says it is not empirical evidence.
cases.shows_zh: 只有推理：关于所设表示的定理和构造的反例，没有冻结的预测，也没有数据；记录自己说这不是经验证据。

cases.case_en: Six language models, each answering as sixteen described persons, chose between two plans for a river, a town or a coast, each plan keeping some of six named things and ending the rest for good.
cases.case_zh: 六个语言模型各扮十六种立场的人，在两个方案之间选择：一条河、一个镇或一段海岸，每个方案保住六样东西中的几样，其余永远终止。

things.thing_en: a valuer: one of six language models answering under one of sixteen standpoint prompts (96 in all)
plan 1 and plan 2 of a decision (112 pairs: widenings W1, W2, W1X; mixed pairs M0, M1, M2; keep pairs K)
the six named formations of a decision (animal populations, plants and habitats, institutions, practices, heritage, enterprises, communities), each continuing or ending for good
the valuer's own lists of what continues under each plan (`continue_1`, `continue_2`)
the sets each plan in fact keeps, computed before any judgment (structure.py)

bridges.name: AI models stand in for valuers (Boundary)
bridges.claim_en: A language model answering under a standpoint prompt is taken as a valuer with an order of its own on outcomes.
bridges.why_en: The record calls the judgments role-play; six families of small models at low reasoning effort are few and may share training, one family is the theory's own, and human valuers remain untested.

bridges.name: T5: every valuer counts everything positively
bridges.claim_en: Each of the 96 valuers is taken as a weighting that counts every listed formation above zero.
bridges.why_en: VD1 did not measure a valuer's sign apart from its ranking. Read after the verdicts, the prompts of standpoints 10 and 15 make an ending a gain; the README says the failure neither confirms nor refutes the exception. VD2 then measured it: gain answers were 0.534 and 0.264 of the answers under those two standpoints.

bridges.name: R1: a judgment's listed sets are its reading
bridges.claim_en: A judgment that lists the two plans' sets correctly is taken as having read the case right.
bridges.why_en: Read after the verdicts by one coder, not blind: 23 of the 121 right-listed W1 and W2 violations describe a trade their own lists do not contain. The study: R1's misread measure, which read the lists, missed them.

bridges.name: locus: weights dispersed (unnamed at the freeze; VT1's RatioWithin)
bridges.claim_en: Valuers are taken to weigh the formations differently enough to split a mixed pair whose larger side keeps one or two more.
bridges.why_en: The valuers mostly count: the larger plan was chosen in 86% of M1 and 90% of M2 judgments. Study §367: the prediction was made without a premise on dispersion.

bridges.name: K1: the order's object
bridges.claim_en: A valuer is taken to compare what each plan keeps, however the plan is worded.
bridges.why_en: Keep pairs, one plan said by what continues and the other by what ends, were called equal in 0.52 of judgments; their read relation was right in 32–90% by model. Cross-framed widenings (W1X) were violated in 12.0% of judgments, against 6.3% for W1.

predictions.label: A1
predictions.says_en: For each model, the narrower plan is chosen in at most 0.03 of its 512 judgments of widening pairs (W1 and W2).

ifs.what_en: every valuer counts every listed formation above zero (the freeze: some standpoints may weigh a formation at zero or below; the theorem binds only positive weightings)

predictions.seen_en: Violation shares: DeepSeek 0.025, GLM 0.041, GPT-6 luna 0.029, Claude Haiku 0.014, Qwen 0.068, Nemotron 0.109; three of six above 0.03: fail. The rules without Claude Haiku, the theory's family, also all fail. Post hoc: the narrower plan was chosen in 41.7% of W1/W2 judgments under standpoint 10 and 14.1% under standpoint 15, at most 4.2% under each other standpoint. Disclosed: the valuers were changed after standpoint 0 on cost alone, no judgment read; another session computed the rules on incomplete rows before the run ended, against the freeze. These verdicts were computed once on the final rows by the unchanged analyze.py; in the early look too every rule failed.
predictions.rival_en: Named in VD2's freeze: a standpoint's pressure on the ranking whatever the valuer's sign; or a misread the lists did not catch.

predictions.label: A2
predictions.says_en: For each model, at most one of the sixteen standpoints chooses the narrower plan more than 2 times among its 32 W1 and W2 judgments.

ifs.what_en: every standpoint counts every listed formation above zero

predictions.seen_en: Standpoints with more than 2: DeepSeek 1, GLM 2, GPT-6 luna 2, Claude Haiku 1, Qwen 2, Nemotron 5; four of six models fail.

predictions.label: R1
predictions.says_en: For each model, among widening judgments (W1, W2, W1X) whose own lists give the true widening, the narrower plan is chosen in at most 0.01.

ifs.what_en: the judgment's own lists give the two plans' sets (taken as reading the case right)
the valuer counts the added formations above zero

predictions.seen_en: 0.029 of 660 (DeepSeek), 0.053 of 641 (GLM), 0.048 of 748 (GPT-6 luna), 0.059 of 752 (Claude Haiku), 0.070 of 643 (Qwen), 0.108 of 678 (Nemotron): every model fails. Post hoc, one reading, not blind: of the 121 W1 and W2 violations whose lists read the widening right, 98 call the ending a gain (92 under standpoints 10 and 15) and 23 describe a trade against their own lists; none gave an order not increasing in admission. Without standpoints 10 and 15 the right-read share is 1.8% in W1 and 0.5% in W2.
predictions.rival_en: The weight below zero was read off prompts and reasons after the verdicts, not measured apart; persona pressure on the ranking would give the same. The lists also missed 23 misreads, so the misread measure did not fully read its construct.

predictions.label: L1 (with L2, L4)
predictions.says_en: At matched sizes mixed pairs are disputed more than widenings: the mean over 16 frames of D(M1) − D(W1) is at least 0.10, and higher in at least 12 of 16 frames.

ifs.what_en: valuers weigh the formation lost against those gained differently enough to split a mixed pair (no premise on dispersion was frozen; read from the share choosing the larger plan, a measurement without prediction)

predictions.seen_en: 0.040, higher in 12 of 16 frames: fail (the frame count met, the mean not). L2 (D(M2) − D(W1) at least 0.05, at least 10 of 16): 0.020, 10 of 16: fail. L4 (L1 on read-right judgments): 0.040, 13 of 16: fail. Mean D: W1 0.063, W2 0.033, M1 0.102, M2 0.082, M0 0.266. The larger plan was chosen in 86% of M1 and 90% of M2 judgments.
predictions.rival_en: Valuers who count: one weight for every formation ranks the larger plan higher in W1, M1, W2 and M2 alike (`Weighting.neutral_ranks_by_number`; the freeze's dry run of counters fails L1 to L4).

predictions.label: L3
predictions.says_en: Pairs decided both ways are the mixed ones: at least 24 of the 48 mixed pairs have D of 0.10 or more, and at most 1 of the 32 widening pairs does.

ifs.what_en: every valuer counts every listed formation above zero

predictions.seen_en: 27 mixed pairs and 4 widening pairs: fail (the mixed clause met, the widening clause not).

predictions.label: K1
predictions.says_en: Two plans that keep the same three formations, one said by what continues and the other by what ends, are called equal in at least 0.70 of judgments: a check that valuers compare what each plan keeps, however it is worded.

ifs.what_en: the valuer reads the two wordings as the same kept sets

predictions.seen_en: Equal in 0.52 of keep judgments: fail. The read relation was right in 32–90% of keep judgments, by model; the README: not called equal largely through misreading.

cases.afterwards_en: By the freeze's 'what would change the account', the locus claim weakened from 'disagreement falls on mixed comparisons' to 'it can fall only there'. VD2, frozen the same day (21 October 2026), measured each valuer's sign apart and named standpoints 10 and 15 in advance. VT1 (22 October 2026) proved in `Becoming.Weightings` what both tests checked (records a-narrowing-above-its-widening and weights-within-a-ratio-agree-past-it), leaving three premises to measure: presentation invariance, the link of a sign measured apart to the joint increment, weight dispersion. T5's claim, standing and refuted-by were rewritten then; T5 now reads 'a bound on where disagreement can fall, not a prediction'. On 9 November 2026 its line was re-said: that actual valuers count every item above zero is what the thesis takes, not shown. No record was made, since no prediction passed.
cases.shows_en: Every frozen rule failed; the theorem's premise, that each valuer counts everything above zero, was not measured apart, and the locus prediction said more than the theorem it rested on.
cases.shows_zh: 冻结的规则全部未过；定理的前提（每个评价者都把每样东西算作正的）没有另外测量，而“分歧落在哪里”的预测说得比它所依的定理多。

cases.case_en: Six language models, each as sixteen described persons, said twice, with no plan shown, whether each named thing's ending is a loss, nothing or a gain, then chose between plans differing by one thing.
cases.case_zh: 六个语言模型各扮十六种立场的人，先在不出示方案时两次回答：每样东西的终止是损失、无所谓还是好处；再在只差一样东西的两个方案之间选择。

things.thing_en: a valuer: one of six language models answering under one of sixteen standpoint prompts (96 in all, VD1's)
the two plans of a one-formation widening, sizes 4 and 3 (96 widenings, each formation the added one once)
the 96 named formations of the sixteen decisions
the valuer's two answers on one formation's ending, no plan shown (serious loss, slight loss, neither, slight gain, serious gain)
the valuer's weight on the added formation when it ranks the pair, shown only by its choice
the valuer's own lists of what continues under each plan, and its stated reason
the sets each plan in fact keeps
two judge models (Gemini 3.8 flash, DeepSeek v4.1 flash) that say whether a reason is inconsistent with the plans

bridges.name: AI models stand in for valuers (Boundary)
bridges.claim_en: A language model answering under a standpoint prompt is taken as a valuer.
bridges.why_en: The record calls the judgments role-play; one of the six families is the theory's own; human valuers remain untested.

bridges.name: V2: the signs are a measurement
bridges.claim_en: A valuer's two answers on a formation's ending, given with no plan shown, are taken as a stable measurement of its sign on that formation.
bridges.why_en: Each model's two elicitations agreed on loss against not-loss in 0.86–0.93 of its cells, above the frozen 0.80; they agree in class in 87.1% of cells and in level in 74.7%.

bridges.name: the link, where the sign is strongly positive (later the hypothesis of Becoming.Weighting.reads_increment)
bridges.claim_en: A loss called twice with no plan shown, at least once a serious one, is taken as a weight above zero on that formation when the valuer ranks the pair.
bridges.why_en: X1s passed for all six models and X2 passed (0.086 against 0.2); study §367 reads these as the link holding where the sign was strongly positive. Where the loss was only slight, X1 failed for one model of six, which the freeze reads as neither a counterexample nor support.

bridges.name: the link, where the sign is a gain
bridges.claim_en: A gain measured apart is taken as a weight below zero on that formation when the valuer ranks the pair.
bridges.why_en: X3: the narrower plan was chosen in 0.490 of 339 such rankings against a frozen 0.50 (0.634 of 213 without Claude Haiku); the README: a separate evaluation is not the weight of a joint ranking (Hsee 1996), chiefly for Claude Haiku.

bridges.name: S2: the other fourteen standpoints
bridges.claim_en: Each standpoint other than 10 and 15 is taken as valuing the formations positively or at zero.
bridges.why_en: Gain shares were 0.063 under standpoint 4 and 0.101 under standpoint 6 against a frozen 0.05.

bridges.name: the judges' misread calls
bridges.claim_en: A choice of the narrower plan whose reason both judges call inconsistent with the plans is taken as a misread.
bridges.why_en: The judges were fixed before the run by calibration on VD1's 121 coded violations (together 114 of 121, κ 0.82), blind to signs and standpoints. A random 16 of their 50 calls in P, read by the session after the verdicts, were all misreads. They called 73 of 428 exact-read violations misread, and each call shrinks the forbidden cell.

bridges.name: exact lists and the judges as the reading
bridges.claim_en: A ranking that lists both plans' sets exactly, and whose reason the two judges do not both call inconsistent, is taken as read right.
bridges.why_en: Read after the verdicts: several of Nemotron's and GLM's violations in P describe a trade the plans do not contain, which the judges did not call; Claude Haiku's six X1s′ cases on VD1's rankings misdescribe cross-framed plans, also not called.

predictions.label: X1
predictions.says_en: Per model: among exactly read one-formation widenings whose added formation's ending the valuer twice called a loss (P), the narrower plan is chosen, not judged misread, in at most 0.01.

ifs.what_en: both askings called the added formation's ending a loss, slight or serious
the ranking lists both plans' sets exactly, and a choice of the narrower counts unless both judges call its reason inconsistent
the sign given with no plan shown is the sign of the valuer's weight within the pair

predictions.seen_en: DeepSeek 0 of 1,057; GLM 9 of 1,011 (0.0089); GPT-6 luna 10 of 1,349 (0.0074); Claude Haiku 0 of 1,207; Qwen 4 of 786 (0.0051); Nemotron 10 of 922 (0.0108): one model of six above 0.01, fail. Post hoc: 22 of the 33 violations sit where the ending was called only a slight loss (1.0% of those cases, against 0.26% where it was once a serious loss); 11 are under standpoints 10 and 15. Without the judges X1 would fail for GLM (1.9%), luna (1.9%) and Nemotron (3.7%). One Nemotron presentation was retried without the seed, by a run note landed before the call.
predictions.rival_en: The freeze: borderline valuations measured with noise, neither a counterexample nor support. Post hoc: persona pressure on the ranking at small valuations (luna's seven under the urban planner); misreads the judges did not call.

predictions.label: X1s
predictions.says_en: Per model: the same where at least one of the two askings called the ending a serious loss (PS): the narrower plan in at most 0.01.

ifs.what_en: both askings called the ending a loss, at least one a serious loss
the ranking lists both plans' sets exactly, and a choice of the narrower counts unless both judges call its reason inconsistent
the sign given with no plan shown is the sign of the valuer's weight within the pair

predictions.seen_en: DeepSeek 0 of 815; GLM 5 of 766 (0.0065); GPT-6 luna 0 of 709; Claude Haiku 0 of 819; Qwen 2 of 504 (0.0040); Nemotron 4 of 579 (0.0069): pass for all six. Without the judges X1s would fail for GLM (1.3%) and Nemotron (2.4%). Secondary X1s′ on VD1's rankings: Claude Haiku 6 of 386 (0.0155) fails, all six cases cross-framed widenings; the other five pass.
predictions.rival_en: In the freeze's dry runs, valuers who call every ending a loss and rank by number also pass X1 and X1s (they fail S1); every pair here has sizes 4 and 3. The record adds that agreement could come from training common to current models.

predictions.label: X2
predictions.says_en: Within valuers, choices of the narrower plan fall where the valuer's own sign is not positive: the Mantel–Haenszel risk ratio of a non-misread violation, strongly positive against not positive, stratified by valuer, is at most 0.2.

ifs.what_en: each model's two askings agree on loss against not-loss in at least 0.80 of its cells (V2)
at least 30 violations among valuers that have both cells

predictions.seen_en: 0.086 (75 valuers with both cells, 227 violations): pass. The narrower plan, not misread, was chosen in 0.26% of strongly positive cells and 18.9% of not-positive cells.
predictions.rival_en: None is named for the pass. The freeze's dry runs put persona pressure that ignores the sign at a ratio of about 1 (0.99–1.03), which this is not. Study §367: the tests mostly checked consistency on AI personas whose judgments are role-play.

predictions.label: X3
predictions.says_en: Where both askings called the ending a gain (G2), the valuer chooses the plan that ends it in at least 0.50 of exactly read widenings. The freeze: T5 requires only the first two claims (X1, X2); this one makes the exception explanatory.

ifs.what_en: both askings called the added formation's ending a gain
the sign given with no plan shown is the sign of the valuer's weight within the pair (read from X3's own result, not checked apart)

predictions.seen_en: 0.490 of 339: fail. Without Claude Haiku: 0.634 of 213. Post hoc: Claude Haiku holds 126 of the 339 and chose the narrower plan in 24.6%; under standpoints 10 and 15 the share is 55%, elsewhere 20%.
predictions.rival_en: The record's reading: a separate evaluation is not the weight of a joint ranking (Hsee 1996); these valuers' rankings favour the wider plan more than their separate signs do.

predictions.label: S1
predictions.says_en: Standpoints 10 (the urban planner) and 15 (the engineer), named before any call, each give a higher share of gain answers than every other standpoint.
predictions.seen_en: 0.534 and 0.264; the next is 0.101 (standpoint 6): pass.
predictions.rival_en: The record's self-review: the two were named from VD1's violations, so the pass shows the sign task finds what the rankings showed, not a blind guess.

predictions.label: S2
predictions.says_en: Every other standpoint's share of gain answers is at most 0.05; standpoints 6 and 12 were named before the run as most at risk.
predictions.seen_en: Standpoint 4 (the Buddhist nun): 0.063; standpoint 6 (the libertarian): 0.101; standpoint 12: 0.048: fail. Post hoc: standpoint 4's gains are mostly Claude Haiku's (29% of its answers), standpoint 6's are Nemotron's 27% and GLM's 14%.

cases.afterwards_en: VT1 (22 October 2026) proved in `Becoming.Weightings` what VD1 and VD2 tested. Under a net weighting, a ranking that puts a narrowing above its widening by one item either does not read that pair as the weighting ranks it or has the item at zero or below (`Weighting.narrower_above_net`); read right, it does so exactly where the item weighs below zero (`Weighting.reads_ranksNet`). Read right, where a sign measured apart is the sign of the order's increment in the pair's context, it fixes the ranking (`Weighting.reads_increment`); the witness `Interacting` shows that link is a premise. T5's claim, standing and refuted-by were rewritten then; three premises stay to measure: presentation invariance, that link, weight dispersion. T5's row now carries: X1s and X2 passed, X1 and X3 failed; role-play judgments, human valuers untested. The study leaves open why measured gains are not acted on, and whether that is Claude Haiku's alone. No record was made.
cases.shows_en: With the sign measured apart, the bound held where strongly positive, missed for one model of six as worded, and a measured gain was acted on in 0.490 of cases.
cases.shows_zh: 把正负另外测量之后：强烈为正之处界限成立；按原文措辞，六个模型中有一个超出；测得为“好处”的，只有0.490照此去选。

cases.case_en: For 672 pairs in 270 條, language-model coders count the referents that a classical Chinese 經 and the English chapter's clause each introduce beyond the Lean statement of the same checked theorem.
cases.case_zh: 对 270 條里的 672 对，由语言模型来数：同一条定理，中华本的經和英文本的句子，各比 Lean 陈述多说出几个所指。

things.thing_en: the Lean statement of each declaration (its elaborated type, dumped from the core build with one level of unfolding)
the 中华本's 經 clauses that state the declaration
the canonical English chapter's clause that cites the declaration (E1)
the name table (449 names; each row states the sense taken and the senses not carried, anchored on Lean) and the English glossary; the coders' keys gave the adopted senses and anchors
the two coders: Claude (Opus 5.5), which also wrote both texts, and GPT (gpt-6-astra)
codebook v1.1 and its count X of excess referents (agents X_A, relata X_R, entities X_E), with omissions O, connective mismatches S, predicate excess P

bridges.name: the measure (FIDELITY §1)
bridges.claim_en: The referents a wording introduces that the Lean statement lacks, as a coder counts them, are taken as what the wording smuggles in beyond the checked theorem.
bridges.why_en: No human audit, which the design makes the deciding one; Krippendorff's α on per-segment X was 0.53 on the Chinese side (calibration, after one codebook revision), below the design's 0.8; the design says the measure scores referents, not truth.

bridges.name: WL chapter's claim (a fitting reading layer)
bridges.claim_en: A lower count for the 經 is taken as showing that the classical code, as disciplined by its name table, is a fitting reading layer for this core, the more exact of the two codes compared.
bridges.why_en: The record reads F1 and F2 as supporting this narrower claim on these two texts, LLM-coded and provisional; after ZE it reads the classical code as one fitting instance of a disciplined code, a controlled English being another of about equal measured fidelity. It does not show 'best expression'.

bridges.name: language as the source (FIDELITY §1, the critic reading)
bridges.claim_en: The 經's lower count is taken as belonging to classical Chinese as such, not to how the two texts were written.
bridges.why_en: FC1 separated language neither from the name table's discipline nor from register (full statements against summarizing clauses). The control ZE (23 October 2026), by its registered primary rule, found 經 − CE +0.023, 95% CI [−0.010, +0.055]: does not survive. A second coder leaves −0.27 [−0.50, −0.06] on 60 pairs with the coders' counts unrelated, and the record leaves whether classical Chinese adds anything undecided. The results also cite Becoming.SharedCodes.renamed_carries_iff: nothing in the measure binds the gain to the script.

bridges.name: coder as reader
bridges.claim_en: A language-model coder's count, including the count by the model that wrote the 經, is taken as what a bilingual coder who reads Lean would count.
bridges.why_en: In calibration the Claude coder found no excess referent in any of the 26 經 segments; the GPT coder found some in 10 of them in the table pass and 12 in the naive pass. The record says the data cannot tell a blind spot from over-reading, and reads the main-set 經 figure (0.09) as a lower bound.

bridges.name: Becoming.Web.SelectsThrough (AI reading, D63)
bridges.claim_en: The authoring model coding its own 經 is taken as a selector that marks only what couples into it.
bridges.why_en: Recorded as an open observation, not a result. SC1 (23 October 2026), in English under no name table, found no author-specific deficit (interaction +0.02, 95% interval [−0.05, +0.08]) and a difference of coding threshold; the record says this does not settle it for the 經.

predictions.label: F1
predictions.says_en: The 經 introduce fewer agents (X_A) than the English clauses; refuted if the 95% CI of the mean 經 − English difference lies above 0, supported if below 0, otherwise undecided.

ifs.what_en: The 經 clauses and the English clause are aligned to the same declaration (two coders agreed exactly on 1,303 of 1,399 clauses, κ 0.952; an adjudicator settled the other 96).
A coder from another model family codes both sides (in the main set the GPT coder coded 320 English segments and no 經; both coders coded only the 13 calibration 條 in full).
A bilingual coder who reads Lean audits a 20% sample and every disagreement.

predictions.seen_en: Main set, Claude coder on both sides (672 pairs, 270 條): 經 0.00, English 0.026, difference −0.026, 95% CI [−0.042, −0.013], Wilcoxon p 0.0004; by the plan's consensus score the CI is [−0.05, −0.02]: supported. On the GPT coder's calibration coding: 0 against 0.10, CI [−0.28, 0]: undecided.
predictions.rival_en: The name table's discipline and the full-statement register, not classical Chinese: in ZE the controlled English also had no agents under the Claude coder (0 against 0).

predictions.label: F2
predictions.says_en: The 經 introduce no more excess referents (X) than the English clauses; refuted if the 95% CI of the mean 經 − English difference lies above 0, supported otherwise.

ifs.what_en: The 經 clauses and the English clause are aligned to the same declaration (1,303 of 1,399 clauses agreed, κ 0.952).
No coder sees both wordings of one theorem (separate shuffled packets by language).
Two coders from different model families code every segment (the GPT coder was stopped by direction after 16 of its remaining 59 packets; in the main set it coded no 經).
Coders agree: Krippendorff's α on per-segment X at least 0.8 (Chinese 0.53 on calibration after one revision; English 0.69 on 320 main segments, 0.78 on calibration).
A human audit decides (design §4, F3 of the procedure).

predictions.seen_en: Main set, Claude coder on both sides: 經 0.09, English 0.81, difference −0.71, 95% CI [−0.92, −0.54], Wilcoxon p < 10⁻⁶. By the plan's consensus score: 0.09 against 1.05, −0.96 [−1.18, −0.77]. Calibration (13 條): Claude 0.00 against 1.47, −1.47 [−2.63, −0.54]; GPT 0.58 against 1.61, −1.03 [−1.98, −0.22]. Claude coder, counting matches made only through unfolding as excess: −0.40 [−0.67, −0.14]; negative in 17 of 18 篇, 篇十 at +0.25 over 6 條. Supported, on both coders.
predictions.rival_en: The discipline of the name table and its anchoring, and register (the 經 are full statements, the English clauses summarize), not the language; and the 經's author coding them, so that 0.09 is best read as a lower bound.

predictions.label: F3
predictions.says_en: Omissions (O) are not what buys a lower X: in the genre-matched comparison (經 against the records' English statements, both full statements) the 經 also have lower X and no higher O-rate.

ifs.what_en: F2 holds with a CI below 0 (the plan reads F3 only then).
The genre-matched segments are coded and scored (stopped by direction; the record-law segments already coded are kept and not analysed).

predictions.seen_en: Not measured: by direction of 22 October 2026 the genre-matched segments were stopped before any main result was read. Reported beside it from the main set: O-rate 經 0.18, English 0.42, difference −0.24 [−0.28, −0.20]; the record reads this as omission not lowering the 經's X, with the register difference left standing.

predictions.label: F4
predictions.says_en: The inherited-sense load (X_naive − X_table) is larger for the 經.

ifs.what_en: The naive pass (coders reading without the key) is coded and scored on the main set (stopped by direction).

predictions.seen_en: Not measured: the naive pass was stopped by the same direction; the GPT coder's first 20 naive packets are kept and not analysed.

cases.afterwards_en: 22 October 2026: the codebook was revised once on calibration (v1.1); two plan amendments, made by direction before any main result was read, cut F3 and F4 and stopped the second coder. 23 October 2026: the control ZE was built and run (under the Claude coder the 經's advantage over a controlled English does not survive), and SC1 tested the author-coding observation in English (no author-specific deficit). The WL chapter's claim stands in its narrower form: the disciplined code is a fitting reading layer, the classical code one instance of it; 'best medium' stays untested. 25 October 2026: the record's means were restated as per 條. Still open: a second coder on the main-set 經, a human audit, F3, F4.
cases.shows_en: The predicted direction was seen on two texts; no person audited the count, and it could not tell language from the name table's discipline or from register.
cases.shows_zh: 预测的方向在这两个文本上见到了；但没有人工复核，也分不开起作用的是语言、名表的纪律，还是体裁。

cases.case_en: Bilingual adult readers would learn the same frozen theorems through the classical 經 or a controlled English of equal length and fidelity, then reconstruct unseen systems and handle counterexamples; designed, not run.
cases.case_zh: 让中英双语的成年读者分别用古典的經和等长、等忠实的受控英文学同一批定理，再去重建没见过的系统、处理反例；只有设计，尚未运行。

things.thing_en: the taught theorems of the frozen core: Block D (25 條, 2,406 Han characters of 經) and Block K (23 條, 2,476 characters), five 條 held out in each
the codes: K_zh (the 經 verbatim with 凡例 entries), K_en (controlled English written from the Lean statements and the glossary), and the control arms K_mz, K_en-comp, K_zh-perm
the readers: adult Mandarin–English bilinguals assigned to a code at random (80 per arm, provisional); language models as a separate family
the model notes a reader writes after passes 1, 3 and 10, and the answers on name-free items
the unseen systems shown as diagrams and tables, each answer key checked in Lean
the scores P1 (transfer) and P2 (counterexample handling) at form 3, with the smallest effect of interest 8 points

bridges.name: CL
bridges.claim_en: Readers of the classical code, at equal length and fidelity, are claimed to reconstruct the structure of unseen cases and handle counterexamples better than readers of a controlled English code.
bridges.why_en: The reading test has not been run; the WL chapter lists the claim as untested.

bridges.name: AI reading (DESIGN-H2 §1)
bridges.claim_en: A human reader is taken as a learner working through a class: the code's composition and the reader's prior senses of the characters supply the class, the curriculum the data.
bridges.why_en: The design calls it a correspondence to be tested, not an application of a theorem; if readers do not behave this way the correspondence fails as a model of human reading and no Lean result changes.

bridges.name: H2-L
bridges.claim_en: A code's grouping of its names (by shared characters; by inherited sense kept or stripped) is taken as the lumping its reader learns through, helping where it is the grouping the structure goes alike across.
bridges.why_en: Congruence coding (L1, L2) is specified as mechanical and fixed before data collection; none has been computed or tested.

bridges.name: H2-R (读书百遍)
bridges.claim_en: Rereading identical text is taken as adding no data, so that a gain across passes is the reader changing the class.
bridges.why_en: To be measured through the model notes written after passes; not run.

bridges.name: gates (§2.5)
bridges.claim_en: The arms' texts are taken as equal in length (±5% per block) and in fidelity (back-translation at least 90%; excess referents within 0.1 per statement).
bridges.why_en: No gate has been run. ZE's controlled English is named a candidate for the English code, but it was translated from the 經, where the design has K_en written from the Lean statements and not from the 經.

predictions.label: H2-T (primary)
predictions.says_en: Readers of K_zh beat readers of K_en on transfer (P1) and on counterexample handling (P2), on mechanism-dense text, after the final pass; equivalence within ±8 points, or below −8, on either refutes it.

ifs.what_en: The design is frozen by a commit before any material is shown to a reader (no commit is named).
The four gates pass (length, back-translation fidelity, excess referents and omissions, mechanism density).
Readers meet the pre-tests and have not read the theory, either edition or the repository.

predictions.rival_en: A first-language advantage, compositional coding that any language can carry, or brevity, register and familiarity with the characters: each has a control arm (K_mz, K_en-comp, K_zh-perm). The design says the theory, on its reading, predicts H2-L and not a blanket advantage for one language.

predictions.label: H2-R
predictions.says_en: The K_zh − K_en difference grows over passes: it lies in the slope over forms 1–3, not only in the intercept.

ifs.what_en: Ten passes over ten days on a locked platform, with model notes after passes 1, 3 and 10.

predictions.rival_en: An advantage that does not grow across passes is familiarity or fluency.

predictions.label: H2-A
predictions.says_en: The difference is larger on mechanism-dense text (A) than on conclusion-only text (B) of the same content and length.

ifs.what_en: Mechanism density, rated by three blind raters, exceeds B's in both codes with the A/B ratio agreeing across codes within 10%.

predictions.rival_en: An advantage as large on B as on A does not come from internal generation.

predictions.label: H2-L
predictions.says_en: The difference is concentrated on items where the code's grouping of names agrees with the structure's grouping, and reverses where they disagree.

ifs.what_en: A human reader learns through a class that the code's composition and the reader's prior senses supply (the design's AI reading; it says the theory then predicts H2-L).
Congruence of each item is coded mechanically before data collection (L1 by adjusted Rand index of shared characters against shared Lean constants; L2 from the name table's 古/复/新 column).

predictions.label: Stage-2 controls (K_mz, K_en-comp, K_zh-perm)
predictions.says_en: K_zh beats each of three controls: controlled modern Chinese, English carrying the classical composition in its morphology, and the 經 under an injective renaming of its names; a control within 8 points of K_zh counts as non-inferior.

ifs.what_en: The renaming in K_zh-perm is injective, so the content is unchanged (renaming invariance, the two theorems named) while the code's grouping and the names' inherited senses are destroyed.
Stage-2 arms are run (80 readers each, text A only).

predictions.rival_en: K_mz non-inferior: a first-language advantage. K_en-comp non-inferior: compositional coding any language can carry. K_zh-perm non-inferior: the names' composition and senses do no work.

cases.afterwards_en: The design (22 October 2026) was not frozen: no freezing commit is named, and a run needs its own board claim. Of the folder's two designs only the companion fidelity measure ran (FC1, 22 October 2026); ZE (23 October 2026) built a controlled English edition named as a candidate for the test's English code. The WL chapter keeps H2 and 'classical Chinese is the best medium' as untested. The design states that no theorem changes under any verdict: readings and chapter prose would.
cases.shows_en: A reading of theorems as a model of human readers, with its refuting results written down in advance; designed, not frozen, not run, so the data say nothing yet.
cases.shows_zh: 把定理读作人类读者的模型，并事先写明什么结果会推翻它；只有设计，没有冻结，也没有运行，数据还什么都没说。

cases.case_en: The 經 of all 394 條 were rendered clause by clause into English under an English name table of the same discipline, and language-model coders counted excess referents on FC1's same 672 pairs.
cases.case_zh: 把 394 條的經逐句译成守同样名表纪律的英文，再由语言模型用同样的办法，在 FC1 的那 672 对上数多出的所指。

things.thing_en: the Lean statements of the same declarations (FC1's table, one level of unfolding)
the 經 segments, with FC1's codings (644 segments, 618 in the main set)
the controlled English (CE) segments: the English of the same clauses (1,698 clauses), translated from the 經 with the Lean as a key to the reading
the English name table (names-en.tsv, 449 rows: an English name, the sense taken, what it does not carry, the same anchors)
the coders: Claude (Opus 5.5) on every pair; GPT (gpt-6-astra) on 60 main-set pairs in 55 條
the count X under codebook v1.1 and the registered rule: survives, reversed, or does not survive

bridges.name: the control (ANALYSIS-PLAN)
bridges.claim_en: A difference remaining between the 經 and the controlled English is taken as language plus translation; a vanished one as discipline plus register.
bridges.why_en: CE renders the same clauses against the same declarations, in the same register, under a name table of the same discipline, by the same author family; the plan fixed this reading before any coding of CE was read. Discipline and register are not separated by it.

bridges.name: CE as the 經's twin
