bridges.claim_en: The controlled English is taken as the same statements as the 經, differing only in language.
bridges.why_en: CE is a translation made with the Lean as a key, so renderers could resolve from the Lean what the 經 leave to the reader (one reports doing so for 九·二十八's third clause); the name table was written by one agent in one pass and reviewed only by its checker; a CE written directly from the Lean was not built.

bridges.name: coder as reader
bridges.claim_en: A coder's count of excess referents is taken as the wording's excess.
bridges.why_en: On the 60 pairs both coded, Krippendorff's α on X is 0.03 on the 經 and −0.01 on CE (on omissions 0.64 and 0.73); the primary coder is of the family that wrote both texts; there is no human audit, so neither coder's threshold is shown right.

bridges.name: Becoming.SharedCodes.renamed_carries_iff
bridges.claim_en: The classical names and their English counterparts are taken as a one-to-one renaming, which carries the same law, so that nothing in the measure binds the gain to the script.
bridges.why_en: The results say the theorem already made this likely and that the control confirms it for the Claude coder; the GPT coder leaves a residual for the 經. Whether a translation is a renaming in the theorem's sense is not examined, and the plan itself names no theorem.

predictions.label: Primary (Claude coder, main set, X)
predictions.says_en: Checked: whether the 經's advantage in excess referents holds against English under the same discipline and register. It survives if the 95% CI of the mean per-條 difference 經 − CE lies below 0; above 0 it is reversed; otherwise it does not survive.

ifs.what_en: CE and the 經 are paired on identical clauses and identical Lean statements.
The plan and the scorer were committed before any coding of CE was read (9811339e2).

Both sides are coded by the same procedure (each CE coding agent coded four or five packets in sequence, seven agents, where FC1's 經 were coded one packet per agent; one agent saw another's excess totals without opening its files).
The coder's count is right (the coder is of the family that wrote both texts; no human audit).

predictions.seen_en: 672 pairs in 270 條: 經 0.095, CE 0.071, 經 − CE +0.023, 95% CI [−0.010, +0.055]; Wilcoxon on the 34 條 with a nonzero difference p 0.04, toward more excess in the 經; agents 0 against 0, CI [0, 0]; McNemar on X ≥ 1: 31 pairs with excess only in the 經, 18 only in CE (p 0.09); by 篇 positive in 7, zero in 7, negative in 4. By the registered rule: does not survive.
predictions.rival_en: Translation with the Lean as a key could lower CE's count where the 經 leave a reading open; and this coder finds almost nothing on either side (means 0.05 and 0.07 per segment on the 60 cross-checked pairs).

predictions.label: Cross-family (GPT coder, 60 pairs, X)
predictions.says_en: The same rule on a stratified sample of 60 main-set pairs coded by a coder of another model family; by the plan a check for direction and for the authoring-coder concern, not a second primary test.

ifs.what_en: The two coders' counts of excess agree on these pairs (α 0.03 on the 經, −0.01 on CE).
The GPT coder's threshold on English names is right.

predictions.seen_en: GPT coder: 經 0.61, CE 0.88, 經 − CE −0.27, 95% CI [−0.50, −0.06]: survives, at about a third of a referent per pair, mostly in entities (X_E −0.25, CI [−0.44, −0.06]); agents 0 against 0.055, CI [−0.145, 0]. Claude on the same pairs: 0.055 against 0.073, −0.018 [−0.055, 0]. Mean of the two: 0.33 against 0.48, −0.15 [−0.26, −0.04].
predictions.rival_en: The GPT coder's threshold, not language: SC1 found it lists more excess everywhere, in part numerals the codebook matches; its four agent referents in CE are 'a self' and 'the center', whose excluded senses the key shown to coders does not give.

predictions.label: CE − E1 (discipline in English)
predictions.says_en: If the primary does not survive and the 95% CI of CE − E1 lies below 0, discipline and register account for the advantage on this core, and nothing in the data binds it to classical Chinese.

ifs.what_en: CE and the English chapter's clauses (E1) are coded by the same coder under the same codebook.
Discipline is separated from register (CE matches the 經 in both; the genre-matched comparison was not run).

predictions.seen_en: Claude coder: CE 0.071, E1 0.808, CE − E1 −0.736, 95% CI [−0.942, −0.566]; the share of FC1's advantage that discipline in English recovers, reported beside it, is 1.03 (95% CI [0.98, 1.09]). Exploratory, after reading, GPT coder on 36 pairs: 經 0.36, CE 0.80, E1 1.64; share 0.66, CI [0.11, 0.88].
predictions.rival_en: Register rather than discipline: the two are not separated. CE also inherits the 經's content as its translation.

cases.afterwards_en: 23 October 2026: the WL chapter's open item and testing section were reworded: the measured exactness comes mainly from the name table's discipline and full statements, a controlled English under the same discipline being another fitting reading layer; whether the language adds anything is left undecided, since it depends on the coder. FC1's record had its scope and next step updated the same day and a new record (fidelity-under-one-discipline) was added. Still open: a controlled English written from the Lean, the separation of discipline from register, a human audit or adjudication of the coders' disagreement.
cases.shows_en: Under the same discipline in English, the 經's advantage did not survive for the primary coder and survived for the other; their counts were unrelated, so language stays undecided.
cases.shows_zh: 英文也守同样的名表纪律后，按主比较的编码者，經的优势不再存在；另一个编码者仍见到一点；两者的计数互不相关，语言有没有另加什么，定不下来。
